definition_zh: 咽炎；咽喉炎
definition_en: an inflammation of the pharynx, the passage at the back of the mouth, which makes the throat sore
core_image: 喉咙深处像被火烤过一样通红、干痛，吞咽时一阵刺痛
scene: 冬天感冒后，她的嗓子又红又肿，连咽水都疼。The doctor said the pain came from pharyngitis and told her to rest her voice.
sceneCN: 这里 pharyngitis 是「咽炎」（第 1 个义项：咽部粘膜发炎、咽喉疼痛的病症）；句意：医生说疼痛来自咽炎，并让她少说话、让嗓子休息。

pos.zh: 咽炎；咽喉炎

derivatives.zh: 希腊语 pharynx 直接借入，指「咽」，即口腔后方的通道
pharynx 加 -eal，指「咽的；咽部的」，名词形式为 pharyngitis 的词干
同一 -itis 后缀加 larynx（喉），指「喉炎」，与咽炎常同时出现

senses.title: A sore, inflamed throat
senses.definition: an inflammation of the pharynx that causes a sore, dry or scratchy throat
senses.definitionCN: 咽部发炎，导致嗓子疼痛、干燥或发痒
senses.example: She stayed home for two days because of pharyngitis.
senses.exampleCN: 因为咽炎，她在家待了两天。
senses.why: The Greek stem pharyng- names the throat passage, and -itis marks inflammation, so the word says exactly what it is.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词干 pharyng- 指咽部通道，-itis 标记炎症，所以这个词直接说出了它是什么。

senses.title: Infection of the throat by a germ
senses.definition: a throat infection caused by a virus or bacterium, often with fever and swollen glands
senses.definitionCN: 由病毒或细菌引起的咽喉感染，常伴发热与淋巴结肿大
senses.example: The test confirmed that his pharyngitis was caused by a bacterium.
senses.exampleCN: 检测确认他的咽炎由细菌引起。
senses.why: Since most throat inflammation comes from germs, the medical word often carries the cause as well as the symptom.
senses.whyCN: 由于多数咽部炎症源自病原体，这个医学词常常连病因一并带上。

senses.title: A clinical or test finding
senses.definition: a finding of red, swollen throat tissue recorded by a doctor during an examination
senses.definitionCN: 医生检查时记录下的咽部组织发红、肿胀的表现
senses.example: Pharyngitis appeared in the notes beside a raised white cell count.
senses.exampleCN: 病历记录里写着咽炎，旁边是升高的白细胞数。
senses.why: In clinics the word also names what an examiner sees, turning the illness into a recorded sign.
senses.whyCN: 在诊室里，这个词也指检查者看到的表现，把病症变成了一条记录。

intro.en: Pharyngitis is a modern medical coinage from Greek pharynx, the throat, plus the Latinised suffix -itis for inflammation.
intro.cn: pharyngitis 是现代医学新造词，由希腊语 pharynx（咽）加上拉丁化的炎症后缀 -itis 构成。

items.en: Pharynx names the throat, and some scholars connect it with pharanx, a cleft or chasm.
items.cn: 希腊语 pharynx 指喉咙，一些学者认为它与 pharanx（裂缝、深谷）相关，但这一联系存疑。

items.en: Latin borrows the word as pharynx and keeps the medical sense of the throat passage.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 pharynx 借入该词，保留了「咽喉通道」这一医学含义。

items.en: The combining stem pharyng- is fixed in anatomical writing from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 解剖学著述自十六世纪起固定使用词干 pharyng-。

items.en: Medical writers add the suffix -itis, already standard for inflammation, to pharyng-.
items.cn: 医学写作者在 pharyng- 后加上已表示炎症的 -itis，造出这个词。

items.en: English adopts pharyngitis along with the rest of clinical disease names in -itis.
items.cn: 英语大量采用以 -itis 结尾的临床病名，pharyngitis 就在其中。

items.en: Today the word appears in public health advice next to the plain phrase sore throat.
items.cn: 今天这个词常与通俗的「嗓子疼」并列出现在公共健康建议中。

note.en: Pharyngitis shares its -itis ending with a whole family of inflamed-body-part words and sits near the everyday sore throat.
note.cn: pharyngitis 与一整族「身体部位加炎症」的词共享 -itis 词尾，并与日常说法「嗓子疼」相邻。

entries.definition: the passage at the back of the mouth leading to the throat and lungs
entries.definitionCN: 咽：口腔后方通往喉与肺的通道

entries.definition: relating to the pharynx
entries.definitionCN: 咽的；咽部的

entries.definition: inflammation of the larynx, causing a hoarse or lost voice
entries.definitionCN: 喉炎：喉部发炎，导致声音嘶哑或失声

entries.definition: inflammation of the tonsils, often with the same sore throat
entries.definitionCN: 扁桃体炎：扁桃体发炎，常伴同样的嗓子疼

entries.definition: an illness caused by germs entering the body
entries.definitionCN: 感染：病原体侵入身体引起的疾病

entries.definition: a condition in which part of the body becomes red, hot and swollen
entries.definitionCN: 炎症：身体某部分发红、发热、肿胀的状态

normalIntro.en: Pharyngitis is built like a label: pharynx is the place, -itis is the fire, so the word says a burning throat.
normalIntro.cn: pharyngitis 像一张标签：pharynx 是地方，-itis 是火，于是这个词说的就是「着火的喉咙」。

normal.en: The -itis pattern is a rule, not a guess: appendicitis, bronchitis and laryngitis all mean inflammation.
normal.cn: -itis 是规则而非猜测：appendicitis、bronchitis、laryngitis 都表示炎症。

normal.en: Pharyng- keeps the y of pharynx, as in pharyngeal and pharyngitis, so the y is a marker of the family.
normal.cn: pharyng- 保留 pharynx 中的 y，如 pharyngeal 与 pharyngitis，这个 y 就是词族的标记。

normal.en: Strep throat is the everyday name for bacterial pharyngitis in many schools.
normal.cn: 在很多学校，strep throat 就是细菌性咽炎的通俗叫法。

normal.en: The long spelling splits neatly into pharyng and itis, so pronounce the fire at the end.
normal.cn: 长拼写可以干脆地拆成 pharyng 与 itis，重音落在末尾的「火」上。

normal.en: Compare pharynx and larynx: pharynx is wider and higher, larynx makes the voice.
normal.cn: 对比 pharynx 与 larynx：咽更宽更高，喉则负责发声。

abstract.en: Picture a red inner surface at the back of an open mouth, glowing like hot metal.
abstract.cn: 想象张开的嘴深处那片内膜通红，像烧热的金属一样发亮。

abstract.en: Imagine a burning line running from the back of the nose down into the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一条火线从鼻后一路烧到胸口。

abstract.en: Think of a doctor tapping the throat with a small light and writing a single Latin word.
abstract.cn: 想象医生用小灯照着喉咙，然后写下了一个拉丁词。

examples.en: The nurse asked whether the child had pharyngitis or simply a cold.
examples.cn: 护士询问孩子得的是咽炎还是普通感冒。

examples.en: Acute pharyngitis usually clears up within a week.
examples.cn: 急性咽炎通常一周内就会好。

examples.en: He drank warm honey water to ease the pharyngitis.
examples.cn: 他喝温蜂蜜水来缓解咽炎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法人急忒难受」——咽部发炎的人着急又难受，即咽炎；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pharynx（咽、喉咙）→ 拉丁语 pharynx → 解剖学词干 pharyng- → 新拉丁语加 -itis（炎症）→ 英语 pharyngitis。同根词有 pharyngeal；-itis 一族还有 bronchitis、laryngitis、tonsillitis。pharynx 的词源一般认为与 pharanx（深谷、裂缝）有关，但这一点存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Pharyngitis names the inflamed throat, the germ behind it, and the sign a doctor records; all three hang on the same -itis fire.
sensesIntro.cn: pharyngitis 指发炎的咽、背后的病原体，以及医生记录的体征，三者都挂在同一处 -itis 的火上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the back of the open mouth glowing red and dry, painful even to swallow.
core.cn: 核心意象：张开的嘴深处通红发干，连吞咽都疼。

branches.en: The symptom sense puts the inflamed throat first.
branches.cn: 症状义先把发炎的咽放在最前面。

branches.en: The infection sense looks for the germ that started the fire.
branches.cn: 感染义去追问是谁点起了这场火。

branches.en: The clinical sense turns the fire into a line in the notes.
branches.cn: 临床义把这场火变成病历里的一行字。

branches.en: What the patient feels and what the doctor records are two views of one throat.
branches.cn: 病人感到的与医生记录的，是同一条喉咙的两个视角。

branches.en: A germ is found, named, and entered, so infection and diagnosis meet in one test.
branches.cn: 病原体被发现、命名、写下，感染与诊断在一次检测中相遇。

intro.en: Pharyngitis is Greek pharyng- plus the medical suffix -itis, the same pattern behind dozens of inflammation names.
intro.cn: pharyngitis 由希腊词干 pharyng- 与医学后缀 -itis 组成，几十个炎症病名都遵循同一模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin took pharynx from Greek unchanged, and built the adjective pharyngeus on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样借入希腊语 pharynx，并在同一词干上造出形容词 pharyngeus。

items.meaning: throat, the passage behind the mouth
items.example: The stem pharyng- points to a place in the body.
items.exampleCN: 词干 pharyng- 指向身体的一个部位。

items.example: Pharynx is the place named by the word.
items.exampleCN: pharynx 是这个词所指的部位。

items.example: The suffix -itis is the fire in every name of this type.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -itis 是这类病名中的那团火。

items.example: Place plus fire gives the diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 部位加火，就是诊断。

items.example: The suffix -eal forms pharyngeal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eal 构成 pharyngeal。

items.example: Pharyngeal describes the throat area.
items.exampleCN: pharyngeal 描述咽部。

items.example: The root laryng- maps the neighbouring part.
items.exampleCN: 词根 laryng- 标出相邻的部位。

items.example: Laryngitis uses the same suffix one step lower.
items.exampleCN: laryngitis 用同一后缀，指向下方一个部位。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms pharyngitic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 pharyngitic。

items.example: Pharyngitic names the condition of the patient.
items.exampleCN: pharyngitic 指病人所处的状况。

definition_zh: 恐惧症；强烈而无理的畏惧；排斥情绪
definition_en: a strong and lasting fear of something that is out of proportion to the real danger
core_image: 有人在关门时手抖得钥匙对不准锁孔，那扇门在眼里变成了一头会扑过来的兽
scene: 地铁车厢越来越挤，她手心出汗，只想逃回地面。Her phobia about crowded trains keeps her off the underground.
sceneCN: 这里 phobia 是「恐惧症」（第 1 个义项：对特定事物的病理性怕）；句意：她对拥挤列车的恐惧症让她不敢坐地铁。

pos.zh: 恐惧症；对某事物的病理性强烈恐惧
强烈而持久的厌恶或排斥
构词成分：与名词结合表示「……恐惧」，用于心理学术语

derivatives.zh: 由词尾 -ic 构成，义为「恐惧症的；恐惧的」
带 -ic 的形容词兼作名词，指「患恐惧症的人」
构词成分，接在名词后表示「对……的恐惧」，如 claustrophobia
构词成分，表「害怕……的人」，如 Anglophobe

senses.title: A lasting clinical dread
senses.definition: a persistent and excessive fear of a particular object or situation that is recognized as irrational
senses.definitionCN: 对特定物体或情境的持久且过度的恐惧，患者自己也知道这种怕不合情理
senses.example: Her phobia started after a terrifying lift accident.
senses.exampleCN: 她的恐惧症始于一回可怕的电梯事故。
senses.why: Greek phobos means flight and the panic that drives it, so a phobia is the body fleeing an object it has marked as dangerous.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phobos 既指逃遁也指促人逃遁的惊惶；恐惧症就是身体对某个被标为危险的物体夺路而逃，医学把这份惊慌固定到单一对象上。

senses.title: Fear as a named condition
senses.titleCN: 对某事物之怕；被命名的怕
senses.definition: a strong irrational fear treated as a recognizable condition with a name of its own
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一种有专名、可辨认的病态之怕来对待的强烈非理性恐惧
senses.example: Doctors now treat flying phobia as separate from ordinary nerves.
senses.exampleCN: 医生如今把飞行恐惧与一般的紧张区别开。
senses.why: Because Greek phobos could be pinned to an object with a compound, medicine could name each dread as its own disease.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phobos 本可与具体对象拼成复合词，医学因此能把每一种怕都命名成一种独立的病。

senses.title: Strong distaste without terror
senses.definition: an intense dislike that is stronger than ordinary dislike but need not involve panic
senses.definitionCN: 比普通讨厌强烈得多、却未必伴随惊恐的厌恶
senses.example: Some analysts describe the firm as suffering from a phobia about risk.
senses.exampleCN: 有分析师说这家公司患上了风险厌恶症。
senses.why: Once phobia meant any flight from a thing, a business or a public mood could show the same rushing away, without a doctor involved.
senses.whyCN: 当 phobia 泛指导任何躲避，商界或公众情绪也能表现出同样仓皇的躲闪，不必真有人在看医生。

senses.title: The -phobia suffix
senses.definition: an element attached to nouns in technical words to name the fear of the thing named
senses.definitionCN: 在技术术语中接在名词后面，表示「对……的怕」的构词成分
senses.example: Xenophobia and hydrophobia both carry the old Greek ending.
senses.exampleCN: xenophobia 与 hydrophobia 都带着古老的希腊语词尾。
senses.why: The suffix is the frozen Greek noun, kept as a building block so that any feared thing can be named.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀就是被冻结下来的希腊语名词，被留作构件，于是任何招人怕的东西都能被命名。

senses.title: Adjective and noun partner
senses.definition: the derived word phobic, used as an adjective for the fear or as a noun for the person
senses.definitionCN: 派生词 phobic：可作形容词修饰该恐惧，也可作名词指患恐惧症的人
senses.example: Its phobic patients avoid lifts whenever they can.
senses.exampleCN: 它接诊的恐惧症患者只要有办法就避开电梯。
senses.why: The -ic ending turns the Greek noun into a Latin-shaped adjective, and English then lets the adjective stand alone for the sufferer.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ic 把希腊名词变成拉丁式形容词，英语再让这个形容词单独作名词指患者。

intro.en: Phobia comes from Greek phobos, fear, through Latin and French phobia, and is now also a combining form.
intro.cn: phobia 源自希腊语 phobos（恐惧），经拉丁语与法语的 phobia 进入英语，如今还兼作构词成分。

items.en: The root is reconstructed as bhegw, to run, source of the Greek noun for fear.
items.cn: 一般认为词根是重构形式 bhegw，意为奔跑，是希腊语「恐惧」名词的来源。

items.en: Phobos names flight, panic, and the terror sent by a god.
items.cn: phobos 指逃遁、惊惶，也指神所降的恐怖。

items.en: Second-element compounds such as hydrophobia already name a specific dread.
items.cn: 古希腊语里已有 hydrophobia 这类以 phobos 作后项的复合词，专门指某种怕。

items.en: Latin poetry keeps phobus as a borrowed form for fear or panic.
items.cn: 拉丁语诗歌借用 phobus 一形表示恐惧与惊惶。

items.en: Phobie is used for a fear that has become pathological.
items.cn: 十九世纪法语 phobie 用来指已经病理化的恐惧。

items.en: Phobia settles as a clinical noun and a productive suffix.
items.cn: 现代英语里 phobia 定型为临床名词，并成为能产的后缀。

note.en: Group one holds the family built on the Greek fear word; group two holds ordinary English fear words.
note.cn: 第一组是建在希腊语「恐惧」上的词族；第二组是英语里普通的「怕」字。

entries.definition: relating to a phobia, or a person who has one
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧症的；恐惧的；患恐惧症的人

entries.definition: the Greek noun for fear and flight behind the word
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语 phobos 是同源原词，意为恐惧与逃遁

entries.definition: fear of enclosed spaces, built with the same ending
entries.definitionCN: 幽闭恐惧症，用同一个词尾构成的复合词

entries.definition: the general feeling of being afraid, reasonable or not
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧，泛指害怕，可合理也可无理

entries.definition: great fear of something that is coming
entries.definitionCN: 对将要发生之事的深恐

entries.definition: a broad uneasy worry rather than a fear of one thing
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑，是对整体的不安，而非对某个单一事物的怕

normalIntro.en: Phobia is Greek fear that has been given a name and made to stay.
normalIntro.cn: phobia 是被命名的希腊语「怕」，而且赖着不走。

normal.en: The Greek noun phobos also names panic and flight.
normal.cn: 希腊语名词 phobos 也指惊惶与逃遁。

normal.en: Use a phobia about or a phobia of to name the feared thing.
normal.cn: 用 a phobia about 或 a phobia of 引出所怕之物。

normal.en: Social phobia and claustrophobia are fixed medical labels.
normal.cn: social phobia 与 claustrophobia 都是固定的医学标签。

normal.en: Compare fear: fear can be sensible, a phobia is not.
normal.cn: 对比 fear：fear 可以合理，phobia 则不合理。

normal.en: Link it to xeno- and homo- cousins that also fear something.
normal.cn: 联想 xeno- 与 homo- 这类同样带「怕」的同族词。

abstract.en: Picture a lift door closing while a shadow waits inside.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯门合拢，里面有一个影子在等。

abstract.en: Imagine a medical chart with one word printed on every page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张病历，每一页只印着同一个词。

abstract.en: Think of a whole boardroom backing away from a single risk chart.
abstract.cn: 想象整个会议室的人一齐躲开一张风险图表。

examples.en: She has a phobia of enclosed spaces.
examples.cn: 她有幽闭恐惧症。

examples.en: Phobias can often be treated with gradual exposure.
examples.cn: 恐惧症常常可以通过逐渐接触来治疗。

examples.en: His fear of failure had become something like a phobia.
examples.cn: 他对失败的怕已经变得近乎一种恐惧症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「服气啊」——明明服气这地方没危险，脚却先替你跑开，这就是 phobia（恐惧症）；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 phobos（恐惧、逃遁、惊惶）→ 拉丁语与法语 phobia → 英语 phobia，核心义「对某一对象的怕，而且怕到要跑」。

sensesIntro.en: Phobia starts as clinical dread of one thing, gains named compounds, then relaxes into strong distaste and a suffix.
sensesIntro.cn: phobia 从对单一事物的临床恐惧出发，长出一串命名的复合词，再放宽为强烈反感，最后定型为构词成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that looks like a beast about to spring.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门在眼里变成会扑过来的兽。

branches.en: Clinical dread is the founding sense.
branches.cn: 临床上的恐惧是基本义项。

branches.en: A named condition lets each dread stand alone.
branches.cn: 被命名的病症让每种怕独立成条。

branches.en: Strong distaste drops the panic but keeps the retreat.
branches.cn: 强烈反感去掉了惊恐，留下了退避。

branches.en: A dread with a name is what a clinic records.
branches.cn: 有专名的怕是门诊要记录的东西。

branches.en: General distaste and the suffix both widen the word.
branches.cn: 一般反感与构词成分都拓宽了这个词。

intro.en: Greek phobos supplies the noun, and -ic, -phobe, and -phobia build the family around it.
intro.cn: 希腊语 phobos 提供名词，-ic、-phobe 与 -phobia 在其四周搭起词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phobos means fear, deimos means dread, and stegos means roof.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phobos 表恐惧，deimos 表畏惧，stegos 表屋顶。

items.example: Phobos names the fear itself.
items.exampleCN: phobos 指向恐惧本身。

items.example: The suffix names each feared thing in turn.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀逐一指称每一种所怕之物。

items.example: The -phobe ending marks the person.
items.exampleCN: -phobe 标记的是人。

items.example: The -phobic ending makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: -phobic 构成形容词。

items.example: Phobic describes the state.
items.exampleCN: phobic 描述这种状态。

items.example: Claustro- adds the closed space.
items.exampleCN: claustro- 添上封闭空间。

items.example: Xeno- adds the stranger.
items.exampleCN: xeno- 添上外来者。

items.example: Hydro- adds water.
items.exampleCN: hydro- 添上水。

items.example: Acro- adds the height.
items.exampleCN: acro- 添上高处。

definition_zh: 音位学；音位系统；音位分析
definition_en: the study of the distinctive sound units of a language and of how they pattern together
core_image: 同一把琴键按不同方式分组，分组线落在哪里，听者听到的调子就不同
scene: 老师让学生把一组音逐个替换，看哪一个换掉之后词义就变了。In phonemics, swapping one sound can change the meaning of a word.
sceneCN: 这里 phonemics 是「音位学」（第 1 个义项：研究一个语言里能辨义的音及其组合的学问）；句意：在音位学里，替换一个音可能会改变词义。

pos.zh: 音位学；音系学分支（研究能辨义的音单位）
（某语言的）音位系统；音位总数
音位分析；把语音切分为音位的做法

derivatives.zh: 由 phonemics 去掉 -s 并以 -ic 收尾，义为「音位的；音位学的」
在 phonemic 后加 -ally，义为「按音位地」
基础名词，义为「音位」，phonemics 研究的就是它
学科后缀，把 phonemic 变成「……学」，与 linguistics 同型

senses.title: The science of sound units
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that studies the sound units of a language and their system
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中研究一种语言的音单位及其系统的分支
senses.example: Phonemics asks which sounds count as the same sound.
senses.exampleCN: 音位学要问的是哪些音在听者耳中算作同一个音。
senses.why: The -ics ending makes a science out of phonemic, and the science is the search for units that the language treats as the same.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ics 把 phonemic 变成一门学问，而它所追的正是语言视为同一的那些单位。

senses.title: A language seen as sounds
senses.definition: the actual inventory of distinct sound units that a particular language uses
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定语言实际用到的区别性音单位的总表
senses.example: Spanish phonemics lacks the English vowel in ship.
senses.exampleCN: 西班牙语的音位系统里没有英语 ship 里的那个元音。
senses.why: Once the method existed, each language could be given its own description, so phonemics came to mean the inventory itself.
senses.whyCN: 方法一旦确立，每种语言都能拥有一份自己的描述，phonemics 于是也指那张音位清单。

senses.title: The method of phonemic analysis
senses.definition: the analytical procedure of finding minimal pairs and setting up phonemes from recorded speech
senses.definitionCN: 从录音材料出发，用最小对立组确立音位的分析程序
senses.example: Her fieldwork began with phonemics before any grammar work.
senses.exampleCN: 她的田野工作先做音位分析，再谈语法。
senses.why: Since phonemes cannot be heard directly, the word also names the procedure of proving them by contrast.
senses.whyCN: 音位无法直接听见，所以这个词也指用对比来证明它们的那套程序。

senses.title: Contrast with phonetics
senses.definition: the level of sound study that deals with meaningful sound rather than with physical sound
senses.definitionCN: 语音研究里处理「有意义的音」而非「物理的音」的那个层次
senses.example: Phonetics records the sound, phonemics decides whether it matters.
senses.exampleCN: 语音学记录声音，音位学判断它是否重要。
senses.why: Both words start with phone, but -etics watches the mouth while -emics watches the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 两个词都以 phone 开头，但 -etics 看着嘴的动作，-emics 看着意义。

senses.title: Phonemics as a school
senses.definition: the tradition of analysis associated with the American structuralists, which treats phonemes as bundles of features
senses.definitionCN: 与美国结构学派相关的那套做法，把音位当作若干区别特征的聚合
senses.example: Old textbooks still use phonemics to mean the structuralist style of analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 老教材仍用 phonemics 指结构学派的分析路数。
senses.why: The name travelled with the method, so a whole style of work is known by it.
senses.whyCN: 名字跟着方法走，于是整套做法都以它命名。

intro.en: Phonemics joins Greek phone, voice, with the suffix -emic, itself made from -eme and -ic.
intro.cn: phonemics 把希腊语 phone（声音）与后缀 -emic 连起来，而 -emic 本身由 -eme 与 -ic 组成。

items.en: Phone names the voice or the sound of the voice.
items.cn: 古希腊语 phone 指嗓音或人声。

items.en: Phoneme first means no more than a sound or a tone.
items.cn: 古希腊语 phonema 最初只表示「一个声音」。

items.en: Latin keeps phone and phonema as learned borrowings.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 phone 与 phonema 作为学术词。

items.en: Phoneme is coined in French linguistics for a distinct sound unit.
items.cn: 十九世纪法语语言学造出 phoneme 一词，指区别性音单位。

items.en: The suffix -eme is extended to -emic, and phonemics names the new discipline.
items.cn: 英语把 -eme 扩展成 -emic，并用 phonemics 命名这门新学科。

note.en: Group one holds the phoneme family and its neighbouring field; group two holds the other levels of language.
note.cn: 第一组是音位词族与相邻的学科；第二组是语言研究的其他层次。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of sound that can change a meaning
entries.definitionCN: 音位，即能改变词义的最小音单位

entries.definition: relating to phonemes or to phonemics
entries.definitionCN: 音位的；音位学的

entries.definition: the study of sound systems, of which phonemics is a part
entries.definitionCN: 音系学，音位学是它的一个分支

entries.definition: the study of speech sounds as physical events
entries.definitionCN: 语音学，研究的是物理层面发出的语音

entries.definition: the study of word forms rather than sounds
entries.definitionCN: 形态学，研究词形而非语音

entries.definition: the study of sentence structure
entries.definitionCN: 句法学，研究句子结构

normalIntro.en: Phonemics is the -ics science of phonemes, built by analogy with phonetics and linguistics.
normalIntro.cn: phonemics 是以 -ics 结尾的一门学问，研究对象是 phoneme，构法照 phonetics 与 linguistics。

normal.en: A phoneme is a sound that can change a word.
normal.cn: 音位是能改变词义的声音单位。

normal.en: Phonetics records the sound, phonemics decides what it carries.
normal.cn: 语音学记录声音，音位学判断它承载什么。

normal.en: The -ics ending makes every word of this shape a discipline.
normal.cn: 这类以 -ics 结尾的词都是学科名。

normal.en: Minimal pairs are the test that sets up phonemes.
normal.cn: 最小对立组是确立音位的检验。

normal.en: Compare phonology, the wider system that contains phonemics.
normal.cn: 对比 phonology：那是包含音位学的更大系统。

abstract.en: Picture keys on a piano carrying a card with a letter each.
abstract.cn: 想象琴键上各贴着一张写字母的卡片。

abstract.en: Imagine the letter cards being re-cut and taped back up.
abstract.cn: 想象那些字母卡片被重新裁切又贴回去。

abstract.en: Think of a field notebook full of pairs written side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一本写满成对词形的田野笔记。

examples.en: She published two papers on the phonemics of her dialect.
examples.cn: 她发表了两篇关于自己方言音位系统的论文。

examples.en: Phonemics and phonetics are taught as separate courses here.
examples.cn: 这里的音位学与语音学是分开开课的。

examples.en: The book explains phonemics through minimal pairs.
examples.cn: 这本书通过最小对立组讲解音位学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分你谜」——把一串语音分你一份名单，谜底就是哪些音算数，所以 phonemics 是音位学；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 phone（声音）＋ phonema（一个音）→ 法语 phoneme（音位）→ 英语加 -ic 与学科词尾 -s，即 phonemics（音位学）；核心义「研究语音里哪些差别才算数」。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a discipline, then the inventory that discipline describes, then the procedure it uses, then the level it works at.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指一门学科，再指该学科描述的音位清单，然后是它所使用的方法，最后是它工作的那个层次。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: keys regrouped by hand, so the same sounds now come out differently.
core.cn: 核心意象：琴键被人重新分组，同一批声音听起来就不同了。

branches.en: The discipline is the first and widest sense.
branches.cn: 学科义是最先也最宽的一项。

branches.en: The discipline is then named for the inventory it finds.
branches.cn: 学科名继而转指它找到的音位清单。

branches.en: The word also stands for the method of proof.
branches.cn: 这个词也指那套证明方法。

branches.en: The boundary against phonetics defines the field.
branches.cn: 与语音学的分界定义了这个领域。

branches.en: Method and school are named with the same word.
branches.cn: 方法与流派共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Greek phone gives the sound, -eme gives the unit, and -ics makes the discipline.
intro.cn: 希腊语 phone 给出声音，-eme 给出单位，-ics 使之成为学科。

latinIntro.en: Greek phone is a voice, phonema one sound, and logos a word or account.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phone 表声音，phonema 表一个音，logos 表言词与论说。

items.example: Phone is the sound at the bottom of the word.
items.exampleCN: phone 是这个词最底的「声音」。

items.example: Phonema is the older ancestor of phoneme.
items.exampleCN: phonema 是 phoneme 更早的祖先。

items.example: The -eme ending cuts units out of a stream.
items.exampleCN: -eme 把连续的音流切成单位。

items.example: Phoneme is what the -ics studies.
items.exampleCN: phoneme 正是这门学科的研究对象。

items.example: The -ic ending builds the adjective.
items.exampleCN: -ic 构成形容词。

items.example: The -ics ending names the field.
items.exampleCN: -ics 命名这门领域。

items.example: Phonemic marks a contrast of meaning.
items.exampleCN: phonemic 标记的是意义上的对比。

items.example: The adverb adds -ally.
items.exampleCN: 副词再加 -ally。

items.example: Phonetics is the twin of phonemics.
items.exampleCN: phonetics 是 phonemics 的孪生词。

definition_zh: 语音的；语音学的；与发音有关的；（拼写）表音的
definition_en: relating to the sounds of speech or to the way speech sounds are studied and written down
core_image: 一只手贴在喉头，喉咙的振动与唇齿的开合被直接写成一串符号
scene: 词典在每个词后面印出一串符号，标出它该怎么读。The dictionary prints a phonetic transcription beside every headword.
sceneCN: 这里 phonetic 是「语音的」（第 1 个义项：与语音或发音有关的）；句意：词典在每个词目旁印出语音转写。

pos.zh: 语音的；发音的；语音学的
（拼写）表音的；拼音的
（用语境中的）语音学；音标体系

derivatives.zh: 在 phonetic 后加 -ally，义为「按发音地；从语音上看」
由 phonetic 加 -ian 构成，指「语音学家」
把语音研究作为学科，即「语音学」
加否定前缀 non-，义为「不表音的；拼写与读音不一致的」

senses.title: To do with speech sounds
senses.definition: relating to the sounds of human speech as they are produced and heard
senses.definitionCN: 与人类语音的产生和听觉有关的
senses.example: The phonetic features of the dialect differ from the standard.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言的语音特征与标准语不同。
senses.why: From Greek phone, voice, so the adjective marks whatever belongs to the breath that becomes speech.
senses.whyCN: 源自希腊语 phone（声音），这个形容词指向一切属于那股化为话语的呼吸的东西。

senses.title: Spelling that follows sound
senses.definition: of a spelling system in which letters stand for sounds in a regular way
senses.definitionCN: 指字母按规律代表声音、拼写与读音一致的书写系统
senses.example: English spelling is famously not phonetic.
senses.exampleCN: 英语拼写出了名地不表音。
senses.why: Because the adjective is about sound, a script that follows sound rather than memory is called phonetic.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个形容词说的是声音，一套跟着声音而非跟着记忆走的文字就被称作表音的。

senses.title: The alphabet of speech
senses.definition: relating to the special symbols used to write speech sounds exactly
senses.definitionCN: 指精确记录语音的专用符号体系及用其写下的转写
senses.example: Every entry carries a phonetic transcription in brackets.
senses.exampleCN: 每个词条后面都附有方括号里的语音转写。
senses.why: Phoneticians needed a script with one sign per sound, so the adjective attached itself to the symbols.
senses.whyCN: 语音学家需要一音一符的写法，于是这个形容词也粘到了符号上。

senses.title: The science itself
senses.definition: the study of speech sounds, often named with the singular-looking form
senses.definitionCN: 研究语音的学问，常以单数形式出现
senses.example: Phonetic is not studied here; the department covers phonology instead.
senses.exampleCN: 这里不研究语音学，系里开设的是音系学。
senses.why: The adjective can carry the noun of the discipline, a common drift in the names of sciences.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可以承担学科的名词，这在学科名称里很常见。

senses.title: Filed by ear
senses.titleCN: 按读音归档的；音似检索
senses.definition: arranged by how a name sounds rather than by its spelling
senses.definitionCN: 按名字的读音而非拼写来排列
senses.example: The archive keeps a phonetic index beside the alphabetical one.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆在字母索引之外另备一份按读音排列的索引。
senses.why: The same sound-based logic that names a script also names an index ordered by ear.
senses.whyCN: 命名文字的那种「以声为准」的逻辑，同样用来给按耳朵排序的索引命名。

intro.en: Phonetic reaches English through Latin phoneticus from Greek phonetikos, from phone, the voice.
intro.cn: phonetic 经拉丁语 phoneticus 来自希腊语 phonetikos，源头是 phone（声音）。

items.en: Phone names the voice or the sound of the voice.
items.cn: 古希腊语 phone 指嗓音或人声。

items.en: Phonetikos means fitted for speaking, or skilled in the voice.
items.cn: phonetikos 意为适于发音的、善于用声的。

items.en: Latin phoneticus carries on the Greek meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语 phoneticus 承袭希腊义。

items.en: Phonetique is used for the science of speech sounds.
items.cn: 十九世纪法语 phonetique 用来指研究语音的学问。

items.en: Phonetic covers sounds, spelling, and the international symbols.
items.cn: 现代英语里 phonetic 涵盖语音、拼写与音标。

note.en: Group one holds the -etic family built on the Greek voice; group two holds neighbouring words about sound and speech.
note.cn: 第一组是建在希腊语「声音」上的 -etic 词族；第二组是邻近的谈声音与口语的词。

entries.definition: the science of speech sounds
entries.definitionCN: 语音学，研究语音的学科

entries.definition: in a way that follows speech sounds
entries.definitionCN: 从语音上看；按发音地

entries.definition: a specialist in speech sounds
entries.definitionCN: 语音学家

entries.definition: relating to sound units that carry meaning
entries.definitionCN: 音位的，指承载意义区别的语音单位

entries.definition: spoken rather than written
entries.definitionCN: 口头的，按说而不按写

entries.definition: relating to physical sound waves
entries.definitionCN: 声学的，指物理意义上的声波

normalIntro.en: Phonetic comes from the Greek voice and covers sounds, spelling that follows sound, and the alphabet of speech.
normalIntro.cn: phonetic 出自希腊语的「声音」，涵盖语音、跟随声音的拼写，以及记录语音的字母。

normal.en: The Greek adjective phonetikos meant suited to the voice.
normal.cn: 希腊语形容词 phonetikos 表示适合发声的。

normal.en: Link it to telephone, phonetics, and phoneme.
normal.cn: 把它与 telephone、phonetics、phoneme 连起来。

normal.en: Phonetic spelling follows sound, so it is regular.
normal.cn: 表音拼写跟随读音，因此有规律。

normal.en: A phonetic alphabet needs one sign for each sound.
normal.cn: 音标体系要求每个音对应一个符号。

normal.en: Compare phonemic: that word is about meaning, not sound alone.
normal.cn: 对比 phonemic：那个词关心意义，而不只是声音。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a throat to feel the buzz.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手压住喉咙，感觉那阵振动。

abstract.en: Imagine a mouth on a page pouring symbols into brackets.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴在纸上把符号倒进方括号。

abstract.en: Think of a phone directory read out loud to find a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一本电话簿按读音念出来找人。

examples.en: The teacher gave a phonetic transcription of the word.
examples.cn: 老师给出了这个词的语音转写。

examples.en: Some languages are far more phonetic than English.
examples.cn: 有些语言的拼写比英语表音得多。

examples.en: Any phonetic symbol in the list is read aloud.
examples.cn: 清单里的每个音标都要念出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费耐听」——一个词的读法值得费心耐听，才能记下来，所以 phonetic 与语音有关；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 phone（声音）→ phonetikos（适于发声的）→ 拉丁语 phoneticus → 法语 phonetique → 英语 phonetic，核心义「属于声音、跟着声音走」。

sensesIntro.en: Phonetic begins with speech sounds, extends to spelling that follows them and to the symbols that record them, and then names the science.
sensesIntro.cn: phonetic 先从语音本身出发，延伸到跟随语音的拼写与记录语音的符号，最后借指这门学问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a throat hum turned into exact symbols on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：喉咙的振动被译成纸上一串准确的符号。

branches.en: The plain sense is about sounds themselves.
branches.cn: 基本义就是关于声音本身。

branches.en: Spelling that obeys sound comes next.
branches.cn: 接着是服从声音的拼写。

branches.en: Writing sounds exactly needs symbols of its own.
branches.cn: 精确记录语音需要专用符号。

branches.en: Both look up their entries by sound.
branches.cn: 两者都按声音来查条目。

branches.en: The science gathers the sound, its notation, and its study.
branches.cn: 这门学识把声音、记音与对它的研究收在一起。

intro.en: Greek phone is the root, -etic the adjective ending, and -ics, -ally, and -ian build the relatives.
intro.cn: 希腊语 phone 是词根，-etic 是形容词词尾，-ics、-ally 与 -ian 构建同族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek phone is a voice, phonema one sound, and symphony a sounding together.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phone 表声音，phonema 表一个音，symphony 表一起发声。

items.example: Phone is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: phone 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The -etic ending appears in Greek phonetikos.
items.exampleCN: -etic 出现在希腊语 phonetikos 中。

items.example: Phonetic describes anything about speech sound.
items.exampleCN: phonetic 涵盖一切与语音有关的事物。

items.example: The adverb adds -ally.
items.exampleCN: 副词再加 -ally。

items.example: The -ian ending names the specialist.
items.exampleCN: -ian 命名专门研究者。

items.example: The -ics ending names the science.
items.exampleCN: -ics 命名这门学科。

items.example: Tele- means far, so voice travels.
items.exampleCN: tele- 表远，声音得以远行。

items.example: Sym- means together, with phone.
items.exampleCN: sym- 表共同，与 phone 相连。

items.example: Logos follows the same phone root.
items.exampleCN: logos 接在同一个 phone 词根之后。

definition_zh: 音系学；音位系统；（某语言的）语音系统
definition_en: the study of the sound system of a language, or that sound system itself
core_image: 一整张语音地图：每个声音都有自己的位置与搭档
scene: 语言学课上，老师要求学生先画出这种语言的元音图，再谈音系问题。In the linguistics class, the teacher asked students to draw the vowel chart of the language before discussing phonology.
sceneCN: 这里 phonology 是「音系学」（第 1 个义项：研究某种语言的声音系统）；句意：语言学课上，老师要求学生先画出这种语言的元音图，再谈音系问题。

pos.zh: 音系学；音位系统

collocations.zh: 英语音系；英语音位系统

derivatives.zh: 由词干加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「音系的；音系的」
由 phonological 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在音系上」
由词干加人称后缀 -ist 构成，义为「音系学家」
共享希腊语词根 phone（声音），义为「音位；音素」
共享词干，后缀换成 -etics，义为「语音学」，研究声音本身而非系统

senses.title: The study of sound systems
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that studies how the sounds of a language are organised into a system
senses.definitionCN: 语言学的分支，研究一种语言的声音如何组织成一个系统
senses.example: She is writing a thesis on the phonology of Scottish Gaelic.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在写一篇关于苏格兰盖尔语音系学的论文。
senses.why: The Greek combining part means sound and the suffix means study, so the word was born as the name of a discipline before it named any particular system.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语组合成分意为「声音」，后缀意为「学问」，所以这个词最初就是一门学科的名字，之后才指具体的系统。

senses.title: The sound system of one language
senses.definition: the set of sounds and sound patterns that belong to a particular language or variety
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一语言或某一变体的整套声音与声音模式
senses.example: English phonology allows a cluster like street but not one like ntreet.
senses.exampleCN: 英语音系允许 street 这样的辅音簇，却不允许 ntreet 那样的组合。
senses.why: Once the study named a system, speakers could also use the word for the system inside their own heads.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这门学科为「系统」命名，说话者也开始用这个词指自己脑中那套系统。

senses.title: Sound rules in a specific context
senses.definition: the patterns by which sounds change in particular positions or combinations
senses.definitionCN: 声音在特定位置或组合中发生变化的规律
senses.example: The phonology of the suffix explains why the final sound weakens.
senses.exampleCN: 后缀的音变规则解释了为什么末尾的音会弱化。
senses.why: A system is not a list but a set of regular habits, so the word also names those habits of change.
senses.whyCN: 系统不是一张清单，而是一套有规律的发音习惯，所以这个词也指这些变化的习惯。

senses.title: The phonological shape of a form
senses.definition: the way a particular word or morpheme is shaped in sound within its language
senses.definitionCN: 某个词或语素在其语言中呈现出的声音形态
senses.example: The phonology of the root changes when a prefix is attached.
senses.exampleCN: 加上前缀之后，词根的音系形态就变了。
senses.why: In practical description, linguists speak of the phonology of a single form as shorthand for its sound shape.
senses.whyCN: 在实际描写中，语言学家用「某词形的音系形态」来简指它的声音形状。

intro.en: Phonology joins Greek phone, a voice or sound, with the combining form -logia, a study or discourse.
intro.cn: phonology 由希腊语 phone（声音）与组合成分 -logia（学问、论述）结合而成。

items.en: Phone means a voice or a sound, from the verb phanai, to speak.
items.cn: phone 意为声音、嗓音，来自动词 phanai（说话）。

items.en: The combining part -logia means a study or a body of teaching.
items.cn: 组合成分 -logia 意为学问或一套讲授内容。

items.en: Scholars build Latin-style terms such as phonologia from these Greek pieces.
items.cn: 学者们用这些希腊语成分造出 phonologia 这类拉丁化术语。

items.en: Phonology appears in English in the eighteen hundreds, at first close to phonetics.
items.cn: phonology 在十九世纪进入英语，起初含义与语音学接近。

items.en: The word settles on the study of sound systems, separate from the study of raw sound.
items.cn: 此后该词固定指声音系统的研究，与单纯研究声音本身区分开来。

note.en: Phonology sits beside the phone family of sound words and is often confused with phonetics.
note.cn: phonology 属于以 phone 为核心的声音词族，也常与语音学混为一谈。

entries.definition: the study of seasonal natural events
entries.definitionCN: 物候学，研究季节性自然现象，与目标词只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: relating to sound systems
entries.definitionCN: 与音系有关的

entries.definition: a person who studies sound systems
entries.definitionCN: 研究音系的人；音系学家

entries.definition: the smallest sound unit that distinguishes meaning
entries.definitionCN: 能区别意义的最小声音单位

entries.definition: the study of the physical sounds of speech
entries.definitionCN: 语音学，研究言语的物理声音

entries.definition: the stress, rhythm, and intonation of speech
entries.definitionCN: 韵律，指言语的重音、节奏与语调

entries.definition: the study of how words are built from smaller units
entries.definitionCN: 形态学，研究词如何由更小的单位构成

normalIntro.en: Phonology is the phone study: phone plus -logia, the sound system seen as a field of study.
normalIntro.cn: phonology 是「声音之学」：phone 加 -logia，把声音系统看作一门学问。

normal.en: Phone means sound and -logy means study, so phonology is the study of sounds.
normal.cn: phone 意为声音，-logy 意为学问，所以 phonology 是研究声音的学问。

normal.en: Phonetics studies the sound itself; phonology studies how sounds pattern.
normal.cn: 语音学研究声音本身，音系学研究声音如何组合成模式。

normal.en: The adjective is phonological and the person is a phonologist.
normal.cn: 形容词是 phonological，研究者是 phonologist。

normal.en: A phoneme is the basic unit that phonology organises.
normal.cn: 音位是音系学组织的基本单位。

normal.en: Compare morphology, where -morph- means shape, and phonology, where phone means sound.
normal.cn: 对比 morphology（词形），它的词干 -morph- 意为形状，而 phone 意为声音。

abstract.en: Picture a sound map with every consonant pinned in its own place.
abstract.cn: 想象一张声音地图，每个辅音都被钉在自己的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook that tells a new sound where it may stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，规定一个新声音可以站在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture two neighbouring sounds shifting a little to get along.
abstract.cn: 想象两个相邻的声音为了相处而各自挪动一点。

examples.en: Phonology explains why the plural ending sounds like s in one word and z in another.
examples.cn: 音系学解释了为什么复数词尾在某个词里发 s 音，在另一个词里发 z 音。

examples.en: The phonology of Japanese groups sounds very differently from that of English.
examples.cn: 日语的音系把声音组织的方式与英语很不一样。

examples.en: Students often confuse phonology with phonetics in their first term.
examples.cn: 学生常在第一个学期把音系学与语音学弄混。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛诺乐记」——记住佛号的声音，自然要学会它：声音加学问就是音系学；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 phone（声音、嗓音，源自 phanai，说话）＋ -logia（学问、论述）→ 现代拉丁语 phonologia → 英语 phonology，核心义「声音的系统之学」。

sensesIntro.en: Phonology starts as the name of a discipline, then names the system it studies, then the change rules inside that system, and finally the sound shape of one form.
sensesIntro.cn: phonology 先是学科名，再指它所研究的系统，再指系统内的音变规则，最后指某个词形的声音形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map on which every sound has a place and a partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张地图，每个声音都有自己的位置与搭档。

branches.en: The discipline sense comes directly from the study suffix.
branches.cn: 学科义直接来自「学问」这一后缀。

branches.en: The system sense is what the discipline actually describes.
branches.cn: 系统义正是这门学科所描写的对象。

branches.en: The rule sense shows the system as working habits.
branches.cn: 规则义把系统呈现为运作中的习惯。

branches.en: A single form has its own small map inside the large one.
branches.cn: 单个词形在大地图里有一小块自己的地图。

branches.en: A system and its rules are two views of the same arrangement.
branches.cn: 系统与规则是同一安排的两个视角。

intro.en: Phonology is built from a Greek sound root and a Greek study suffix, with phoneme and phonetics as its neighbours.
intro.cn: phonology 由希腊语的声音词根与「学问」后缀构成，周围有 phoneme 与 phonetics 等词。

latinIntro.en: Through Latinised Greek, phone means sound and -logia means a study or account.
latinIntro.cn: 经由拉丁化的希腊语，phone 意为声音，-logia 意为学问或论述。

items.example: The root phon- appears in many English words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 phon- 出现在许多英语单词中。

items.example: Phone is the Greek noun behind the root.
items.exampleCN: phone 是这一词根背后的希腊语名词。

items.example: The suffix -logy names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -logy 命名一门学问。

items.example: The Greek part -logia is the source of -logy.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语成分 -logia 是 -logy 的来源。

items.example: Phonology names the discipline.
items.exampleCN: phonology 命名这门学科。

items.example: The adjective phonological describes a process.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 phonological 描述一种过程。

items.example: A phonologist compares sound patterns.
items.exampleCN: 音系学家比较声音模式。

items.example: Phoneme shares the same sound root.
items.exampleCN: phoneme 共享同一个声音词根。

items.example: Phonetics studies the sound itself rather than the system.
items.exampleCN: 语音学研究声音本身而非系统。

items.example: The suffix -ics also marks a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ics 同样表示一门学科。

definition_zh: 风景如画的；（言语）生动独特的；古雅有趣的
definition_en: attractive in the way a painted picture would be, or lively and unusual in style
core_image: 一栋老石屋爬满藤蔓，恰好被画框框成一张画
scene: 画家选了一个村口，石墙和藤蔓在夕阳里排成一幅画。The painter chose a village corner where the stone wall and vines made a scene picturesque enough to paint.
sceneCN: 这里 picturesque 是「风景如画的」（第 1 个义项：景物美得像一幅画）；句意：画家选了一个村口，石墙和藤蔓在夕阳里排成一幅画。

pos.zh: 风景如画的；生动独特的；古雅有趣的

collocations.zh: 古意盎然、富有画意的废墟

derivatives.zh: 由目标词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「如画地；生动地」
由目标词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「如画之美」
来自拉丁语 pictura（绘画），义为「图画」，是这个词的构词基础
共享拉丁语词根 pict-（画），义为「图画的；以图画表现的」

senses.title: Looking like a painted picture
senses.definition: charming and beautiful in a way that seems like a painting, usually said of natural or old built scenery
senses.definitionCN: 景物漂亮迷人得像一幅画，多用于自然风光或古老建筑
senses.example: The river winds past a picturesque village.
senses.exampleCN: 河流蜿蜒经过一个风景如画的村庄。
senses.why: The word was borrowed from Italian artists who judged landscapes by whether they were worth painting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词借自意大利画家，他们评判风景的标准是它值不值得入画。

senses.title: Lively and striking in language
senses.titleCN: 生动独特的；形象生动的
senses.definition: used of words or style that are vivid, colourful, and full of striking images
senses.definitionCN: 形容语言或文风鲜明、富于色彩、充满生动的意象
senses.example: She described the storm in picturesque language.
senses.exampleCN: 她用生动独特的语言描写了那场风暴。
senses.why: If scenery can look like a picture, language can paint pictures too, so the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 既然风景能像一幅画，语言也能在听者脑中作画，于是同一个词覆盖了两种对象。

senses.title: Old-fashioned and charming in character
senses.titleCN: 古雅有趣的；别具风味的
senses.definition: having an old-fashioned charm that makes people or things seem quaint and interesting
senses.definitionCN: 带有旧式韵味，使人物场所显得古雅有趣
senses.example: The harbour is full of picturesque fishing boats.
senses.exampleCN: 港口里满是别具风味的老渔船。
senses.why: Painters loved ruins and old corners, so the word grew a fondness for what is worn and quaint.
senses.whyCN: 画家偏爱废墟与老角落，于是这个词也带上了对陈旧古雅的喜爱。

intro.en: Picturesque travels from Italian to French to English, built on Italian pittoresco in the manner of a painter.
intro.cn: picturesque 从意大利语经法语进入英语，源头是意大利语 pittoresco，意为「以画家的方式」。

items.en: Pictura means a painting, and pictor means a painter.
items.cn: pictura 意为绘画，pictor 意为画家。

items.en: Pittoresco describes what looks fit for a painter to paint.
items.cn: pittoresco 形容看上去适合画家去画的东西。

items.en: French takes the word as pittoresque and widens it to scenery.
items.cn: 法语借入该词作 pittoresque，并把适用范围扩大到风景。

items.en: Picturesque enters English as a term in the taste for landscape.
items.cn: picturesque 在十八世纪进入英语，成为风景审美的术语。

items.en: The word extends from landscape to vivid language and quaint old places.
items.cn: 此后该词从风景扩展到生动的语言与古雅的地方。

note.en: Picturesque belongs to the family of picture words and sits near scenic and charming.
note.cn: picturesque 属于以 picture 为核心的词族，并与 scenic、charming 等词相邻。

entries.definition: an image of a person or scene
entries.definitionCN: 图画；照片，是目标词的构词基础

entries.definition: expressed in pictures
entries.definitionCN: 以图画表现的

entries.definition: a rare spelling with extra letters
entries.definitionCN: 一个少见的多字母拼写，只是拼写相近，并非标准词形

entries.definition: in a picture-like way
entries.definitionCN: 如画地；生动地

entries.definition: having beautiful natural views
entries.definitionCN: 景色优美的

entries.definition: very pleasant and attractive
entries.definitionCN: 迷人的；可爱的

entries.definition: peaceful and perfect like a country poem
entries.definitionCN: 田园诗般的；宁静美好的

normalIntro.en: Picturesque is picture plus -esque, in the manner of, so it means shaped like a picture.
normalIntro.cn: picturesque 是 picture 加 -esque（……风格的），合起来就是「像画一样的」。

normal.en: Picture plus -esque gives picturesque, meaning in the manner of a picture.
normal.cn: picture 加 -esque 构成 picturesque，意为「以画的方式」。

normal.en: The suffix -esque comes from Italian and also gives statuesque and grotesque.
normal.cn: 后缀 -esque 来自意大利语，还构成 statuesque 与 grotesque。

normal.en: A picturesque village is one a painter would stop to paint.
normal.cn: 风景如画的村庄就是画家会停下来写生的村庄。

normal.en: Picturesque language paints pictures with words.
normal.cn: 生动独特的语言就是用语词作画。

normal.en: Compare pictorial, which means shown in pictures, and picturesque, which means like a picture.
normal.cn: 对比 pictorial（以图画表现的）与 picturesque（像画一样的）。

abstract.en: Picture a stone house covered in vines inside an invisible frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋爬满藤蔓的石屋，被一个看不见的画框框住。

abstract.en: Imagine hearing a sentence that makes you see a scene.
abstract.cn: 想象听到一句话，却让你看见了一幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture an old boat with peeling paint that tourists love to photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘油漆剥落的老渔船，游人最爱给它拍照。

examples.en: They rented a cottage in a picturesque part of the valley.
examples.cn: 他们在山谷里风景如画的地方租了一间小屋。

examples.en: His letters are full of picturesque details about the market.
examples.cn: 他的信件充满关于集市的生动细节。

examples.en: The old bridge has a picturesque charm that photographs catch well.
examples.cn: 那座老桥有一种别具风味的美，很适合拍照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克雀斯快」——派摄影师带上相机去拍，因为景色太像画；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pictura（绘画，源自 pingere，画）→ 意大利语 pittoresco（以画家方式）→ 法语 pittoresque → 英语 picturesque；词尾 -esque 表示「……风格的」，核心义「像一幅画」。

sensesIntro.en: Picturesque begins with scenery that looks paint-worthy, then passes to language that paints pictures, then to old things loved for their quaint beauty.
sensesIntro.cn: picturesque 先指值得入画的风景，再指能作画的语言，最后指尖旧古雅的景物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked stone wall framed like a finished painting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵歪斜的石墙被框成一幅画。

branches.en: The landscape sense keeps the original painterly judgement.
branches.cn: 风景义保留了最初的「值得入画」的判断。

branches.en: The language sense transfers the paintbrush to words.
branches.cn: 语言义把画笔交到了词句手里。

branches.en: The quaint sense loves what age has softened.
branches.cn: 古雅义偏爱被岁月磨软的东西。

branches.en: Old ruins are picturesque both as scenery and as quaint remains.
branches.cn: 古老废墟既是风景，也是古雅遗迹，因而最有画意。

branches.en: Both senses make ordinary things feel worthy of notice.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让平常之物显得值得一看。

intro.en: Picturesque is picture with the Italian-flavoured suffix -esque, and its relatives are pictorial and picturesqueness.
intro.cn: picturesque 是 picture 加上带意大利风味的后缀 -esque，近亲有 pictorial 与 picturesqueness。

latinIntro.en: Latin pictura, a painting, and pingere, to paint, lie behind the English word picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pictura（绘画）与 pingere（画）是英语 picture 的源头。

items.example: Picture is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: picture 是这个形容词的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -esque means in the manner of.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -esque 意为「以……的方式」。

items.example: Picturesque describes scenery worth painting.
items.exampleCN: picturesque 形容值得入画的风景。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms picturesquely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 picturesquely。

items.example: Picturesquely describes how a place looks.
items.exampleCN: picturesquely 描述一个地方的样貌。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms picturesqueness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 picturesqueness。

items.example: Picturesqueness names the charm itself.
items.exampleCN: picturesqueness 直接命名这种美感。

items.example: Pictorial shares the Latin painting root.
items.exampleCN: pictorial 共享拉丁语「绘画」词根。

items.meaning: to show in a picture or words
items.example: Depict keeps the same painting root with a prefix.
items.exampleCN: depict 带前缀沿用同一绘画词根。

definition_zh: 海盗；盗版者；盗版；非法翻印
definition_en: someone who attacks ships at sea, or someone who copies and sells someone else work without permission
core_image: 一面黑旗在船舷上升起，商船上的水手放下武器
scene: 黑帆船靠上商船，跳帮的人抢走了整箱货物。Armed men jumped aboard the merchant ship and acted like a pirate gang, taking every crate of cargo.
sceneCN: 这里 pirate 是「海盗」（第 1 个义项：在海上袭击船只的人）；句意：黑帆船靠上商船，跳帮的人抢走了整箱货物。

pos.zh: 海盗；盗版者；侵权者
盗版；非法翻印或传播

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词干加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「海盗行为；盗版行为」
由目标词加过去分词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「盗版的」
由词干加形容词后缀 -ical 构成，义为「海盗式的；剽窃的」
由 piratical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以海盗方式」

senses.title: A robber of ships at sea
senses.definition: a person who sails the sea and attacks and robs other ships
senses.definitionCN: 在海上航行、袭击并抢劫其他船只的人
senses.example: In the eighteen hundreds, pirates controlled parts of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪时，海盗控制着部分海岸。
senses.why: Greek peiratai meant men who make an attempt, and the attempt they made on the sea was robbery.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 peiratai 本指「敢于一试的人」，而他们在海上的一试就是抢劫。

senses.title: A copier of protected work
senses.definition: a person or company that copies books, films, software, or music and sells them without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可复制书籍、影片、软件或音乐并加以出售的人或公司
senses.example: The studio sued a pirate who sold the film online.
senses.exampleCN: 制片厂起诉了一名在网上出售该影片的盗版者。
senses.why: The image of taking from others without right transferred from the sea to creative work, so a pirate became anyone who steals ideas or files.
senses.whyCN: 「无权夺取他人之物」的意象从海上转到创作上，海盗就成了偷取创意或文件的人。

senses.title: To copy and sell without permission
senses.definition: to copy and distribute protected material such as software or a film illegally
senses.definitionCN: 非法复制并传播受保护的软件、影片等材料
senses.example: They were caught attempting to pirate the new software.
senses.exampleCN: 他们试图盗版这套新软件时被抓了。
senses.why: When the person noun became a verb, the act of raiding turned into a single illegal copying act.
senses.whyCN: 当人变成动词，抢劫的行为也就浓缩成了一次违法的复制。

senses.title: A broadcaster without a licence
senses.definition: used as an adjective for a station or signal that broadcasts without a legal licence
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指未经合法许可而广播的电台或信号
senses.example: A pirate radio station played records banned by the main channels.
senses.exampleCN: 一家非法电台播放着主流频道禁播的唱片。
senses.why: Modern media use keeps the sea sense of sailing outside the law, now on the airwaves instead of the waves of the sea.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒体用法保留了「在法律之外航行」的意味，只是从海面换到了空中电磁波。

intro.en: Pirate comes through Latin and French from Greek peirates, a sea robber, built on a root meaning to attempt or try.
intro.cn: pirate 经由拉丁语与法语来自希腊语 peirates（海上劫掠者），其词根意为「尝试、冒险」。

items.en: Peirates means a sea robber, formed from peiran, to try or attempt.
items.cn: peirates 意为海上劫掠者，由 peiran（尝试、冒险）构成。

items.en: Pirata keeps the sense of a sea robber in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pirata 保留「海上劫掠者」之义。

items.en: The word reaches Old French as pirate or pirate-like forms.
items.cn: 该词以 pirate 一类形式传入古法语。

items.en: English uses pirate for sea robbers from the late Middle English period.
items.cn: 英语在中古英语后期开始用 pirate 指海上劫掠者。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word spreads to copyright and then broadcasting.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，该词扩展到版权领域，继而用于非法广播。

note.en: Pirate is close to piracy and smuggler in meaning, and to pilot in spelling and sound.
note.cn: pirate 与 piracy、smuggler 意义相近，又与 pilot 拼写、发音相近。

entries.definition: the crime of attacking ships or copying work
entries.definitionCN: 海盗行为或盗版行为

entries.definition: copied illegally
entries.definitionCN: 盗版的

entries.definition: a person who guides a ship or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 领航员；飞行员，与目标词只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a large stone structure with a square base
entries.definitionCN: 金字塔，与目标词仅是首音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who moves goods secretly to avoid tax or law
entries.definitionCN: 走私者

entries.definition: a person who steals by force
entries.definitionCN: 掠夺者

entries.definition: a pirate who attacks ships in the Caribbean
entries.definitionCN: 海盗，尤指在加勒比海劫掠的海盗

normalIntro.en: Pirate carries the Greek sense of an attempt made on the sea, later moved to copying and the airwaves.
normalIntro.cn: pirate 承载希腊语「在海上出手一试」的意味，后来转到复制与电波上。

normal.en: The Greek root means to try, so a pirate is one who tries to take what is not his.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根意为「尝试」，所以海盗就是试图拿走不属于自己之物的人。

normal.en: Piracy is the activity and pirate is the person.
normal.cn: piracy 是行为，pirate 是那个人。

normal.en: Pirate radio sails outside the law, just as a pirate ship did.
normal.cn: pirate radio 就像海盗船一样，在法律之外航行。

normal.en: Pirated films are films copied without permission.
normal.cn: pirated films 就是未经许可复制的影片。

normal.en: Compare pilot, which starts and ends with the same sounds but means a guide, not a robber.
normal.cn: 对比 pilot，它首尾音相同，却指领航者，不是劫掠者。

abstract.en: Picture a black flag rising over the sail of a merchant ship.
abstract.cn: 想象一面黑旗在商船的帆上升起。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of cheap copied films sold in a market.
abstract.cn: 想象市场上摊着一排廉价的盗版影片。

abstract.en: Picture a small radio in a boat playing a banned song.
abstract.cn: 想象船上的一台小收音机播放着禁播的歌。

examples.en: A pirate raised a flag as the ship came into view.
examples.cn: 船影出现时，一名海盗升起了旗帜。

examples.en: Many films are pirated before they even reach the cinema.
examples.cn: 许多影片还没进影院就已经被盗版了。

examples.en: Piracy costs the software industry millions every year.
examples.cn: 盗版每年让软件行业损失数百万。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派瑞特」——派他去抢别人的东西，就是海盗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 peiran（尝试、冒险）→ peirates（海上劫掠者）→ 拉丁语 pirata → 古法语 pirate → 英语 pirate，核心义「在海上出手夺取」。

sensesIntro.en: Pirate begins as the sea robber, moves to the person who copies protected work, then to the act of copying, and finally to unlicensed broadcasting.
sensesIntro.cn: pirate 先是海上劫掠者，再指复制受保护作品的人，随后指复制行为，最后指无照广播。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black flag raised over a boarded merchant ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑旗在被登上的商船上空升起。

branches.en: The sea robber keeps the original Greek sense.
branches.cn: 海盗义保留了最初的希腊语含义。

branches.en: The copier moves the robbery from the sea to creative work.
branches.cn: 盗版者义把劫掠从海上移到创作上。

branches.en: The verb turns the raider into a repeated illegal act.
branches.cn: 动词义把劫掠者变成反复发生的违法行为。

branches.en: Both the ship and the station operate without a licence.
branches.cn: 海盗船与非法电台都无照行事。

branches.en: Copying and broadcasting are the modern seas a pirate sails.
branches.cn: 复制与广播是海盗如今航行的新海域。

intro.en: Pirate is a person noun that became a verb, with piracy and pirated gathered around it.
intro.cn: pirate 原本是人名词，又转为动词，周围聚集着 piracy 与 pirated。

latinIntro.en: Latin pirata came from Greek peirates, and the attempt root behind it means to try.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pirata 来自希腊语 peirates，其背后的「尝试」词根意为试探。

items.example: The root pir- comes from Greek peiran.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pir- 源自希腊语 peiran。

items.example: Peirates is the direct Greek source.
items.exampleCN: peirates 是直接的希腊语来源。

items.example: Pirate keeps the sea sense.
items.exampleCN: pirate 保留了海上含义。

items.example: The verb pirate arrived much later.
items.exampleCN: 动词 pirating 出现得晚得多。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms piracy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 piracy。

items.meaning: the crime of robbing ships or copying
items.example: Piracy names the activity as a whole.
items.exampleCN: piracy 整体地为这一行为命名。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms pirated.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 pirated。

items.example: Pirated describes the copies sold.
items.exampleCN: pirated 描述被出售的副本。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms piratical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ical 构成 piratical。

items.example: Piratical describes behaviour or style.
items.exampleCN: piratical 描述行为或风格。

definition_zh: 雌蕊
definition_en: the female reproductive part of a flower, usually made of a stigma, a style and an ovary
core_image: 花朵中央立着的一支细颈小瓶，顶端接着花粉，底部藏着种子
scene: 植物课上，老师把一朵百合掰开，指着花朵中央那根细长的雌蕊，让学生说出它由哪几部分组成。那根细长的雌蕊就是这节课的主角。In the botany lesson, the teacher opened a lily and pointed at the slender pistil standing in the middle of the flower.
sceneCN: 句意：植物课上，老师把一朵百合掰开，指着花朵中央那根细长的雌蕊，让学生说出它由哪几部分组成。这里 pistil 是「雌蕊」（第 1 个义项：花的雌性生殖器官）。

pos.zh: 雌蕊；花心（植物学）

derivatives.zh: 由 pistil 加形容词后缀构成，义为「有雌蕊的；雌性的」，用于描述只长雌蕊的花
由 pistil 加「-ferous（携带）」构成，义为「生有雌蕊的」，常见于植物志

senses.title: The whole female organ of a flower
senses.definition: the entire female reproductive structure of a flower, made of one or more carpels
senses.definitionCN: 一朵花完整的雌性生殖结构，由一个或多个心皮组成
senses.example: The pistil stands at the centre of the flower.
senses.exampleCN: 雌蕊立在花朵的中央。
senses.why: The name came from the Latin word for a pestle, because the shape of the organ matched the tool used for pounding.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语里「杵」一词，因为雌蕊的形状正好与捣东西用的杵相像。

senses.title: A single carpel seed vessel
senses.definition: one carpel, or one free unit, of a flower that holds the ovules
senses.definitionCN: 花中承载胚珠的单个心皮或单个游离单位
senses.example: A simple pistil consists of just one carpel.
senses.exampleCN: 单雌蕊只由一个心皮构成。
senses.why: Botanists split the organ into units, so one pestle shaped unit is also called a pistil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家把这一器官按单位拆分，所以单独一支杵形的单位也叫雌蕊。

senses.title: The three parts working as one
senses.titleCN: 柱头、花柱与子房的合称
senses.definition: the stigma, the style and the ovary viewed together as a single working system
senses.definitionCN: 把柱头、花柱和子房合起来看作一个整体系统
senses.example: Pollen lands on the top of the pistil and grows down towards the ovary.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉落在雌蕊顶端，并向下长向子房。
senses.why: The pestle image has three parts, a head, a rod and a cup, and each does one step of fertilisation.
senses.whyCN: 杵的意象本身就有三部分：杵头、杵杆和杵臼，而它们各管受精的一个步骤。

senses.title: The carpel as a carpellary leaf in theory
senses.definition: in plant theory, the carpel treated as a modified leaf folded to enclose ovules
senses.definitionCN: 在植物学理论中，被看作一片折叠包裹胚珠的变态叶
senses.example: The pistil is thought to be a folded leaf in botanical theory.
senses.exampleCN: 在植物学理论中，雌蕊被认为是一片折叠而成的叶。
senses.why: Once people explained the pestle like organ as a folded leaf, the name was carried over to that idea.
senses.whyCN: 当人们开始把杵形器官解释成折叠的叶时，这个名字也顺势带到了这个理论概念上。

intro.en: Pistil comes through French from Latin pistillum, a pestle, a small pounding tool, because the flower part is pestle shaped.
intro.cn: pistil 经由法语来自拉丁语 pistillum（杵，一种小型捣击工具），因为雌蕊的形状就是杵形的。

items.en: Pistillum means a pestle or the handle used for pounding in a mortar.
items.cn: pistillum 指杵，即用来在研钵里捣压东西的手柄。

items.en: French botanists borrowed pistil for the central organ of a flower.
items.cn: 法国植物学家借用了 pistil 一词来指花的中央器官。

items.en: English takes pistil into botanical writing, next to stamen, the male part.
items.cn: 英语把 pistil 引入植物学著作，与表示雄性器官的 stamen 并列。

items.en: Linnaeus used the Latin word pistillum, so the English form keeps the Latin silhouette.
items.cn: 林奈采用了拉丁词 pistillum，所以英语词形保留了拉丁语的外形。

items.en: Modern botany keeps pistil for the whole organ and carpel for one unit, though the two are often used loosely.
items.cn: 现代植物学用 pistil 指整个器官，用 carpel 指单个单位，尽管两者常被混用。

note.en: Pistil belongs to the flower family with stamen, carpel and stigma, and it also looks like pistol and pastel.
note.cn: pistil 属花的词族，与 stamen、carpel、stigma 为伴，同时和 pistol、pastel 拼写相近。

entries.definition: a small handgun
entries.definitionCN: 手枪；只是拼写相近，词源不同，pistol 来自中古法语的枪名

entries.definition: a soft pale colour, or a chalk crayon
entries.definitionCN: 淡柔的颜色；彩色粉笔；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a heavy tool for grinding in a mortar
entries.definitionCN: 杵；与 pistil 同出拉丁语 pistillum，正是雌蕊名字的来源

entries.definition: the male part of a flower that makes pollen
entries.definitionCN: 雄蕊；花中产生花粉的雄性部分，与雌蕊相对

entries.definition: one unit of the female organ of a flower
entries.definitionCN: 心皮；雌蕊的组成单位

entries.definition: the tip of the pistil where pollen lands
entries.definitionCN: 柱头；雌蕊顶端接受花粉的部位

normalIntro.en: Pistil is a pestle turned into a flower: a small pounding tool that now holds seeds.
normalIntro.cn: pistil 是杵变成的花：原本用来捣东西的小工具，如今盛着种子。

normal.en: Pistil and pestle share the same Latin source, pistillum.
normal.cn: pistil 与 pestle 同出拉丁语 pistillum（杵）。

normal.en: The pistil is the female part and the stamen is the male part.
normal.cn: 雌蕊是花中偏雌性的部分，雄蕊是雄性部分。

normal.en: The pistil has three parts: stigma, style and ovary.
normal.cn: 雌蕊有三部分：柱头、花柱和子房。

normal.en: Pollination usually means pollen moving from a stamen to a pistil.
normal.cn: 传粉通常指花粉从雄蕊移到雌蕊上。

normal.en: Compare pistol: a pistol is a gun, a pistil is the seed bearing flower part.
normal.cn: 对比 pistol：pistol 是手枪，pistil 是结籽的花器。

abstract.en: Picture a slender flask standing in the middle of a petal ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一支细颈小瓶立在花瓣围成的圆环中央。

abstract.en: Think of one beaker on its own, holding all the seeds inside.
abstract.cn: 把单心皮雌蕊想成一只单独的小烧杯，所有种子都盛在里面。

abstract.en: Watch a pollen grain land on the top and slide down to the bottom cup.
abstract.cn: 看一粒花粉落在顶端，再一路滑到底部的小杯里。

examples.en: A lily has a long pistil with a rounded stigma.
examples.cn: 百合有一根长长的雌蕊，顶端是圆圆的柱头。

examples.en: The pistil receives pollen on its stigma.
examples.cn: 雌蕊在柱头上接收花粉。

examples.en: Bees carry pollen from the stamens to the pistils.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂把花粉从雄蕊带到了雌蕊上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮丝挑」——想象一根细细的皮丝从花心挑出来，那就是雌蕊；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pistillum（杵）→ 法语 pistil（花的中央器官）→ 英语 pistil，核心义「杵形、居中的花器」。

sensesIntro.en: Pistil starts as the whole female organ, splits into single seed units, then into the three working parts, and finally into the old theory that it is a folded leaf.
sensesIntro.cn: pistil 先从整株雌性器官讲起，再拆成单个承载胚珠的单位，然后是三个协同工作的部位，最后落到「雌蕊是一片折叠叶」的旧理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slender pestle standing upright in the centre of a flower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细长的杵立在花朵中央。

branches.en: The whole organ keeps the name, viewed as one central body.
branches.cn: 把整株器官看作一个中央体，沿用了这个名字。

branches.en: Each single unit is one more pestle, a separate seed vessel.
branches.cn: 每个单独单位就是又一支杵，一个独立的承籽容器。

branches.en: Head, rod and cup become stigma, style and ovary.
branches.cn: 杵头、杵杆、杵臼分别对应柱头、花柱和子房。

branches.en: The whole pestle and its three parts are one and the same object.
branches.cn: 整支杵和它的三个部分其实是同一个对象。

branches.en: Theory redraws the pestle shape as a folded leaf.
branches.cn: 理论把杵形重新解释成一片折叠的叶。

intro.en: Pistil is a whole Latin noun, and English builds a small family around it with pistillate and pistilliferous.
intro.cn: pistil 本身就是一个完整的拉丁语名词，英语围绕它用 pistillate 和 pistilliferous 构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pistillum means a pestle, and the plant word keeps the tool image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pistillum 意为杵，表示植物的这个词保留了工具的意象。

items.example: Pistillum is the direct source of the flower name.
items.exampleCN: pistillum 是这一花器名称的直接来源。

items.meaning: the female part of a flower
items.example: Pistil names the organ as a whole.
items.exampleCN: pistil 指整个雌蕊器官。

items.example: Compound flowers may have several pistils.
items.exampleCN: 复合花可能有多个雌蕊。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms pistillate, meaning bearing pistils.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 pistillate，义为长有雌蕊的。

items.example: A pistillate flower has no stamens.
items.exampleCN: 雌花没有雄蕊。

items.example: The suffix -ferous forms pistilliferous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ferous 构成 pistilliferous。

items.example: Pistilliferous appears in older plant descriptions.
items.exampleCN: pistilliferous 出现在较早的植物描述中。

items.example: Pestle is the everyday tool word from the same Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: pestle 是由同一个拉丁名词而来的日常工具词。

items.meaning: the male part of a flower
items.example: Stamen is the paired term for pistil in flower study.
items.exampleCN: stamen 是花部研究中与 pistil 配对的术语。

definition_zh: 可怜的；令人同情的；可悲的；少得可怜的
definition_en: deserving or causing pity; so poor in quality or amount that it seems sad
core_image: 蜷在雨里、浑身湿透的小狗，抬头望着你
scene: 雨下个不停，一只小狗躲在门口发抖，路过的人都停下脚步，看着那个可怜的小家伙。A wet puppy shivered by the door in the rain, and passers by stopped to look at that pitiful little creature.
sceneCN: 句意：雨下个不停，一只小狗躲在门口发抖，路过的人都停下来看那只可怜的小家伙。这里 pitiful 是「令人同情的、可怜的」（第 1 个义项：引发他人怜悯的）。

pos.zh: 可怜的；令人同情的
可悲的；少得可怜的

derivatives.zh: 由 pity 加「-less（没有）」构成，义为「无情的；冷酷的」，与 pitiful 的「有同情」正好相对
由 pitiful 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「可怜；令人同情之处」
由 pity 加形容词后缀 -eous 构成，义为「凄惨的；哀伤的」，多形容声音与表情
pitiful 的基础词，义为「怜悯；同情」

senses.title: Arousing pity in the viewer
senses.definition: so sad or helpless that other people feel sorry for you
senses.definitionCN: 处境悲伤或无助，以至于旁人替你难过
senses.example: The injured bird was a pitiful sight.
senses.exampleCN: 那只受伤的小鸟看上去很可怜。
senses.why: Pity is the feeling of sorrow for someone, and the suffix -ful means full of, so pitiful means full of pity.
senses.whyCN: pity 是为他人的处境而感到难过，词尾 -ful 表示「充满」，所以 pitiful 就是「充满怜悯的」。

senses.title: Deserving of pity, used of a person
senses.definition: used of a person who deserves sympathy or care
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容值得同情或需要照料的某人
senses.example: The pitiful refugees slept under plastic sheets.
senses.exampleCN: 那些可怜的难民睡在塑料布下面。
senses.why: The same feeling is turned towards people, and the word shifts from the sight to the sufferer.
senses.whyCN: 同一种怜悯之情转向了人，词便从「所见之景」移到了「受苦之人」。

senses.title: Inadequate to the point of scorn
senses.definition: of very low quality or amount, so that it invites contempt rather than sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 品质或数量太低，引来的是轻蔑而非同情
senses.example: They offered a pitiful effort to fix the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修路的努力少得可怜。
senses.why: The image of weakness spreads from bodies to effort, money and excuses, and pity turns into scorn.
senses.whyCN: 虚弱的意象从身体扩散到努力、金钱和借口，怜悯也随之变成轻蔑。

intro.en: Pitiful is formed in English from pity and the suffix -ful, and pity goes back through Old French pite to Latin pietas, dutiful devotion.
intro.cn: pitiful 是英语内部用 pity 加后缀 -ful 构成的，而 pity 经由古法语 pite 追溯到拉丁语 pietas（虔敬、尽责的爱）。

items.en: Pietas means dutiful love, loyalty and reverence, first for gods and parents.
items.cn: pietas 意为尽责的爱、忠诚与敬重，最初指向神祇和父母。

items.en: Pietas also takes the sense of compassion and mercy in Christian Latin.
items.cn: 在基督教拉丁语中，pietas 又增添了怜悯与慈悲之义。

items.en: Pite means pity or compassion, and it enters English through this form.
items.cn: 古法语 pite 意为怜悯、同情，英语正是经由这个词形借入的。

items.en: Pity settles as a noun for compassion, and its adjective piteous already exists.
items.cn: pity 作为表示同情的名词固定下来，其形容词 piteous 也已存在。

items.en: Pitiful is built from pity plus -ful, and later gains the mocking sense of inadequacy.
items.cn: pitiful 由 pity 加 -ful 构成，后来发展出带嘲讽意味的「蹩脚、少得可怜」。

note.en: Pitiful shares its root with pity and pitifully, and it sits beside pitiable, pathetic and poor in the field of sympathy.
note.cn: pitiful 与 pity、pitifully 同根，并与 pitiable、pathetic、poor 一起待在「同情」这个语义场里。

entries.definition: sympathy for the suffering of others
entries.definitionCN: 同情；怜悯

entries.definition: in a way that deserves or shows pity
entries.definitionCN: 可怜地；凄惨地

entries.definition: showing no sympathy
entries.definitionCN: 无情的；冷酷的

entries.definition: deserving pity, more restrained in tone
entries.definitionCN: 值得同情的；语气更克制

entries.definition: arousing pity, or so weak as to be sad
entries.definitionCN: 可怜的；也可指可悲的、窝囊的

entries.definition: very unhappy or in very bad conditions
entries.definitionCN: 悲惨的；痛苦不堪的

normalIntro.en: Pitiful is literally full of pity: the heart of the viewer swells when the eyes see suffering.
normalIntro.cn: pitiful 字面就是「满是怜悯」：眼睛看到苦难，旁观者的心便涨满了同情。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, so pitiful means full of pity.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ful 表示充满，所以 pitiful 就是充满怜悯。

normal.en: A pitiful sight makes people feel sorry.
normal.cn: a pitiful sight 是让人心生怜惜的景象。

normal.en: A pitiful excuse is a very weak excuse.
normal.cn: a pitiful excuse 是非常低劣的借口。

normal.en: Compare pitiless, which means without pity at all.
normal.cn: 对比 pitiless：完全没有怜悯、冷酷无情。

normal.en: Piteous describes the sound, pitiful more often describes the whole scene.
normal.cn: piteous 多形容声音，pitiful 更多形容整个场景。

abstract.en: Picture a wet puppy looking up with huge round eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只湿透的小狗抬起圆圆的大眼睛。

abstract.en: See a person huddled under a blanket on a cold night.
abstract.cn: 想象寒夜里有人裹着毯子缩成一团。

abstract.en: Think of an empty plate next to a tiny coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空盘旁只放着一枚小小的硬币。

examples.en: The starving dog looked pitiful in the doorway.
examples.cn: 门口的流浪狗看起来可怜极了。

examples.en: His excuse was so pitiful that nobody believed him.
examples.cn: 他的借口蹩脚得没人相信。

examples.en: The team made a pitiful attempt to save the match.
examples.cn: 这支队伍试图挽救比赛，但表现得十分可悲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「披题服」——披着破题、穿着旧服的人看着可怜，由此记住 pitiful 的「可怜」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pietas（虔敬、尽责的爱）→ 晚期拉丁语「怜悯」→ 古法语 pite → 英语 pity → pity + -ful = pitiful，核心义「充满怜悯」。

sensesIntro.en: Pitiful starts from a sight that fills the viewer with pity, passes to the person who suffers, and finally slides into the scornful sense of being too weak or too small.
sensesIntro.cn: pitiful 先指让人心头一软的画面，再指值得同情的人，最后滑向「太弱太小、令人轻蔑」的贬义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soaked puppy shivering in the doorway, eyes turned up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只湿透的小狗在门口发抖，抬起眼睛望着人。

branches.en: The sight itself is full of pity for those who look.
branches.cn: 景象本身对观看的人而言满是怜悯。

branches.en: The feeling moves from the sight to the person who suffers.
branches.cn: 情感从景象移向受苦的人。

branches.en: Weakness becomes contempt when effort or money falls short.
branches.cn: 当努力或金钱太少时，脆弱就变成了轻蔑。

branches.en: Both the sad scene and its victim draw the same compassion.
branches.cn: 凄惨的场景和其中的受害者激起的是同一种同情。

branches.en: A single word can carry sympathy or scorn, decided by context.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能带同情也能带轻蔑，全由上下文决定。

intro.en: Pitiful is pity plus -ful, and its family runs from the noun pity through pitiable and piteous to the negative pitiless.
intro.cn: pitiful 由 pity 加 -ful 构成，它的词族从名词 pity 出发，经 pitiable、piteous 一直到反义形式 pitiless。

latinIntro.en: Latin pietas gives pity, and the same pietas is behind pious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pietas 给出 pity，它与表示虔诚的 pious 同出一源。

items.example: Pietas carries both devotion and later mercy.
items.exampleCN: pietas 既有虔敬，后来又有怜悯。

items.example: Pite is the form that reached English.
items.exampleCN: pite 是传入英语的词形。

items.example: Pity names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: pity 指这种情感本身。

items.example: The suffix -ful turns pity into pitiful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 把 pity 变成 pitiful。

items.example: Pitiful describes both feeling and weakness.
items.exampleCN: pitiful 既可形容感受，也可形容脆弱。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms pitifulness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 pitifulness。

items.example: The suffix -less forms pitiless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 pitiless。

items.example: Pitiless is the direct opposite of pitiful.
items.exampleCN: pitiless 是 pitiful 的直接反义。

items.example: The suffix -eous forms piteous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eous 构成 piteous。

items.example: Piteous often describes a cry or face.
items.exampleCN: piteous 常形容哭声或面孔。

items.example: The suffix -able forms pitiable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 pitiable。

items.example: Pious comes from the same Latin pietas as pity.
items.exampleCN: pious 与 pity 同出拉丁语 pietas。

definition_zh: 枢轴；支点；核心；围绕……转动；转折；转身；以……为轴
definition_en: a central point on which something turns; to turn around such a point, or to change direction
core_image: 门轴上的合页：门板以它为圆心转开
scene: 木匠把合页固定在门框上，门板便以这根轴为中心开合，每一次转动都绕它进行。The carpenter fixed the hinge to the door frame, and the door now swings on that pivot.
sceneCN: 句意：木匠把合页固定在门框上，门板如今就以这根轴为中心开合，每次转动都绕它进行。这里 pivot 是「枢轴、支点」（第 1 个义项：物体绕之转动的中心轴）。

pos.zh: 枢轴；支点
核心；关键
以……为轴转动；以……为核心
转身；转向

derivatives.zh: 由 pivot 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「关键性的；起枢纽作用的」，由「转轴」引申为「牵一发而动全身」
由 pivot 与 man 复合而成，义为篮球中的「策应中锋」，也泛指核心人物

senses.title: The pin or axis a thing turns on
senses.definition: a short pin or central shaft on which something turns or balances
senses.definitionCN: 物体借以转动或保持平衡的短轴或中心轴
senses.example: The door swings on a brass pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门绕着一根黄铜枢轴开合。
senses.why: The word first named the pin of a hinge, the physical point where turning begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指合页上的销轴，也就是任何转动最早发生的那一点。

senses.title: The central person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing on which a whole activity depends or revolves
senses.definitionCN: 整个活动赖以展开、围绕其运转的人或事物
senses.example: She is the pivot of the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是整个团队的核心。
senses.why: The image of a pin is moved from metal to people, since everything turns around them too.
senses.whyCN: 轴的意象从金属转到了人身上，因为一切也围绕他们运转。

senses.title: To turn on a point
senses.definition: to turn around a central point while staying on one spot
senses.definitionCN: 在一个点不动的前提下绕中心转动
senses.example: The dancer pivoted on one foot.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者以一只脚为轴转身。
senses.why: Once the noun named the axis, the verb named the motion that the axis allows.
senses.whyCN: 名词定下轴线之后，动词就用来表达这条轴所允许的那种运动。

senses.title: To change direction or strategy
senses.definition: to change direction, business or plan without giving up the goal
senses.definitionCN: 在不放弃目标的前提下改变方向、业务或计划
senses.example: The firm pivoted from hardware to software.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从硬件转向了软件。
senses.why: A physical turn becomes a business turn, with the old base kept and the direction changed.
senses.whyCN: 物理的转动变成了经营上的转向，基座留在原处，方向则改了。

senses.title: To depend entirely on
senses.definition: to be decided by, or to rest entirely on, a single factor
senses.definitionCN: 由单一因素决定，或完全悬于其上
senses.example: The whole plan pivots on one successful test.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划取决于一次成功的试验。
senses.why: If everything turns around one point, then everything also hangs on that point.
senses.whyCN: 既然一切都绕一点转动，那么一切也都悬在那一点上。

intro.en: Pivot comes from Old French pivot, a pin or hinge, and the origin of that word is uncertain.
intro.cn: pivot 来自古法语 pivot（销、合页轴），该古法语词更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Pivot means a pin or a hinge on which a door or lid turns.
items.cn: pivot 指门或盖子转动所依托的销子或合页。

items.en: The earlier source of Old French pivot is uncertain, though some link it to a root for piercing.
items.cn: 古法语 pivot 更早的来源不确定，有人认为与表示「刺入」的词根有关，但这只是推测。

items.en: Botanists and builders pick up a similar sounding word for a shaft or a turning point.
items.cn: 博物学家和建筑者采用了读音相近的词，用来指轴或转动的支点。

items.en: English borrows pivot first as a hinge pin and then as any turning point.
items.cn: 英语先把 pivot 用作合页销钉，继而泛指任何转动的支点。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb and the business sense of changing direction, popular in start up talk.
items.cn: 现代英语补上了动词形态，又添加了「转向」的经营义，在创业圈里流行起来。

note.en: Pivot shares a family with pivotal and pivotman, and in meaning it sits close to hinge, axis, fulcrum and revolve.
note.cn: pivot 与 pivotal、pivotman 同族，在意义上又与 hinge、axis、fulcrum、revolve 相邻。

entries.definition: central and very important
entries.definitionCN: 关键性的；起枢纽作用的

entries.definition: a player who sets up moves, or a key figure
entries.definitionCN: 策应中锋；核心人物

entries.definition: a bush often used for hedges
entries.definitionCN: 女贞（常作绿篱的灌木）；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a joint on which a door turns
entries.definitionCN: 铰链；合页；最接近实物意义的近义词

entries.definition: an imaginary line around which a body turns
entries.definitionCN: 轴；物体绕之以转动的假想线

entries.definition: the point on which a lever rests
entries.definitionCN: 支点；杠杆所依托的点

normalIntro.en: Pivot is a hinge seen as a single point: stand on it and everything else turns.
normalIntro.cn: pivot 是把合页看成一个点：你站在上面，其余一切都随之转动。

normal.en: Pivot on comes from turning on a hinge, and means to depend on.
normal.cn: pivot on 由绕合页转动而来，表示取决于。

normal.en: Pivotal keeps the turning image and carries the idea of being crucial.
normal.cn: pivotal 保留了转动的意象，带上「至关重要」之意。

normal.en: A pivot point is the point where the direction of a move changes.
normal.cn: pivot point 是移动方向发生改变的那一点。

normal.en: In basketball the pivot foot must stay on the floor.
normal.cn: 篮球里的中枢脚必须始终贴地。

normal.en: In modern business, to pivot is to change direction while keeping your goal.
normal.cn: 在现代商业中，pivot 指的是在保留目标的同时改变方向。

abstract.en: Picture a gate swinging easily on a single pin.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在一根销轴上轻快地开合。

abstract.en: See a compass needle spinning around its centre.
abstract.cn: 想象指南针的指针绕自身中心旋转。

abstract.en: Think of a dancer turning on one pointed foot.
abstract.cn: 想象舞者以一只脚尖为圆心旋转。

examples.en: The sliding door turns on a metal pivot.
examples.cn: 这扇推拉门绕着一根金属枢轴转动。

examples.en: The whole debate pivots on one question.
examples.cn: 整场辩论都取决于一个问题。

examples.en: The company pivoted to online sales last year.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年转向了线上销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮窝头」——门轴上磨出一个小皮窝头似的凹坑，门就绕它转；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 pivot（销、合页轴）→ 英语 pivot，更古来源不确定；核心义「让万物绕之转动的那个点」。

sensesIntro.en: Pivot moves from the metal pin, to the central figure, to the turning motion, to a change of plan, and finally to dependence on one factor.
sensesIntro.cn: pivot 从金属销轴出发，依次走向中心人物、转动动作、计划转向，最后落到「依赖于某一因素」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge pin on which a heavy door swings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根让沉重门板转动的合页销轴。

branches.en: The physical pin is the oldest and most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 实物的销轴是最早也最具体的义项。

branches.en: The pin becomes a person when everything turns around him.
branches.cn: 当一切都围绕某人运转时，销轴就变成了人。

branches.en: The axis becomes the action, the turning itself.
branches.cn: 从轴线本身过渡到动作，也就是转动本身。

branches.en: Changing direction and depending on one factor are two abstract later turns.
branches.cn: 改变方向与依赖单一因素，都是后来发展出的两个抽象引申。

branches.en: The pin and the turn it allows belong to one mechanical picture.
branches.cn: 销轴和它所允许的转动属于同一幅机械图景。

intro.en: Pivot is a borrowed whole word, and English builds pivotal and pivotman on top of it.
intro.cn: pivot 是整词借入的外来词，英语在它之上又构成了 pivotal 与 pivotman。

latinIntro.en: Pivot has no certain Latin ancestor, though Medieval Latin took a similar form for a turning shaft.
latinIntro.cn: pivot 没有确定无疑的拉丁语祖源，不过中世纪拉丁语借用了读音相近的形式来表示转轴。

items.example: The Old French pivot names the hinge itself.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 pivot 指的就是合页。

items.example: The English noun widens to any turning point.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词扩展到任何转动的支点。

items.example: The verb is used widely in sport and business.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在体育和商业中都用得很广。

items.example: The suffix -al forms pivotal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 pivotal。

items.example: Pivotal describes decisions and people that change everything.
items.exampleCN: pivotal 形容足以改变一切的决定或人物。

items.meaningCN: 表示从事某事之人的复合成分
items.example: The element -man joins pivot to make pivotman.
items.exampleCN: 复合成分 -man 与 pivot 组合成 pivotman。

items.meaning: a key player or central figure
items.example: Pivotman is used of the centre in basketball.
items.exampleCN: pivotman 在篮球里指中锋。

items.example: Pivot point names the exact place where a turn happens.
items.exampleCN: pivot point 精确指出转折发生的位置。

items.meaning: a joint that lets a door turn
items.example: Hinge is the everyday object that a pivot names more precisely.
items.exampleCN: hinge 是日常所说的合页，pivot 指得更精确。

definition_zh: 关键的；起决定作用的；枢轴的；围绕中心转动的
definition_en: extremely important because everything else depends on it, or relating to a central point on which something turns
core_image: 一扇门全靠门轴转动，轴一歪，整扇门就卡住
scene: 谈判整整拖了一夜，所有人都在等一个人的表态。Her vote proved pivotal, and the deal was signed before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 pivotal 是「关键的、起决定作用的」（第 1 个义项：别的结果都取决于它）；句意为她的那一票起了决定作用，协议在黎明前签了下来。整扇门靠一个轴转动，这根轴就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 关键的；起决定作用的；枢轴的

collocations.zh: 在塑造……方面起关键作用

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「枢轴；支点」以及「以……为中心转动」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「关键性地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「关键性；枢轴性」，较少用

senses.title: Decisive for what follows
senses.definition: so important that later events, results or decisions depend on it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到后来发生的事件、结果或决定都要取决于它
senses.example: Her early research was pivotal to the whole project.
senses.exampleCN: 她早期的研究对整个项目起了决定作用。
senses.why: The pivot is the one point a door or beam turns on; move that point and everything around it swings, so pivotal comes to mean decisive for what follows.
senses.whyCN: pivot 是门或梁绕其转动的那一个支点，支点一动，周围的一切都随之摆动，于是 pivotal 引申为「决定后续一切」的关键。

senses.title: A turning point in time
senses.titleCN: 转折点上的；承前启后的
senses.definition: marking a moment or period when a course of events turns in a new direction
senses.definitionCN: 标志着事件走向发生转折的那一刻或那一段时期
senses.example: That summer was a pivotal moment in his career.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天是他事业上的关键时刻。
senses.why: If the pivot is where a thing turns, a pivotal moment is the instant when history or a career turns on that point.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pivot 是物体转动的地方，那么 pivotal moment 就是历史或事业在此转折的那一瞬间。

senses.title: Turning on an axis
senses.definition: turning freely on a central axis, as a part, joint or body does
senses.definitionCN: 像零件、关节或身体那样绕中心轴自由转动
senses.example: The lamp sits on a pivotal base, so it can be aimed anywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯装在可转动的底座上，可以指向任何方向。
senses.why: This is the older mechanical sense: a pivotal joint or wheel is one that pivots, and the figurative senses grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的机械义：pivotal 的关节或轮子就是能 pivot（绕轴转）的部件，比喻义正是从这里长出来的。

intro.en: Pivotal is the adjective of pivot, a word that entered English from Old French in the sense of a hinge pin or axis.
intro.cn: pivotal 是 pivot 的形容词形式；pivot 经古法语进入英语，最初指门铰链上的销轴或转轴。

items.en: Pivot appears in English from about the fifteenth century, named after the pin on which a hinge turns.
items.cn: pivot 约于十五世纪进入英语，得名于铰链转动所依靠的销轴。

items.en: The Old French ancestor is usually given as pivot, but the further origin is disputed.
items.cn: 一般认为来自古法语 pivot，但更早的来源有争议。
