items.en: Some link it to the Latin noun piva, a pipe or peg, but the details are uncertain.
items.cn: 有人认为它与拉丁语 piva（管、钉）有关，但细节来源不确定。

items.en: In the eighteenth century pivot became a general word for a central axle and for a turning movement.
items.cn: 十八世纪，pivot 成为表示中心轴以及转动动作的通用词。

items.en: The adjective pivotal was formed to describe a joint or hinge that turns.
items.cn: 形容词 pivotal 被造出来，用来描述能转动的关节或铰链。

items.en: The figurative sense took over: a pivotal role or a pivotal moment is the hinge of a whole situation.
items.cn: 比喻义后来占了上风：pivotal role 或 pivotal moment 就是整个局面的枢纽。

note.en: The first group gathers the pivot family and look-alike words; the second gathers words that also sit at the centre of importance.
note.cn: 第一组收 pivot 词族与形近词；第二组收同样位于重要性中心的词。

entries.definition: a central pin, axle or point on which something turns, or to turn around one
entries.definitionCN: 基础词，义为「枢轴；支点」以及「以……为中心转动」

entries.definition: supported or turning on a pivot
entries.definitionCN: 由 pivot 加 -ed 构成，义为「绕轴安装的」

entries.definition: a large printed sign carried in a protest; only the spelling looks similar
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标语牌、布告」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: extremely important for an outcome, very close in use to pivotal in British academic writing
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「至关重要的」，在英式学术写作中与 pivotal 十分接近

entries.definition: of decisive importance, and also used of a point where a situation may change sharply
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的」，也用于局面可能急转的那个点

entries.definition: most important and at the centre of a matter, but not necessarily decisive
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中心的、核心的」，强调位置重要，但不一定起决定作用

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pivot family, the hinge image behind the word and the phrases it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的 pivot 词族、词背后的铰链意象以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Pivot is the pin a hinge turns on; pivotal is the hinge itself.
normal.cn: pivot 是铰链转动所依靠的销轴，pivotal 就是整副铰链。

normal.en: Pivotal is pivot plus -al, the usual ending for a related adjective.
normal.cn: pivotal 是 pivot 加 -al，这是构成相关形容词的常见词尾。

normal.en: A pivotal role is the role on which the whole plan turns, as in a pivotal role in the talks.
normal.cn: pivotal role 指整个计划绕其转动的角色，例如「a pivotal role in the talks」。

normal.en: Before pivotal was used for people and events, it described a joint that could turn freely.
normal.cn: 在用来形容人和事件之前，pivotal 描述的是能自由转动的关节。

normal.en: Compare crucial: crucial marks importance, pivotal adds the picture of the hinge.
normal.cn: 对比 crucial：crucial 标记重要性，pivotal 多了一层铰链转动的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door hanging on one small pin; take the pin out and the door falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门挂在一根小销轴上，拔出销轴，门就倒下。

abstract.en: See a road that forks at the very moment you move; that instant is the pivotal moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路就在你迈步的那一刻分叉，那一瞬间就是 pivotal moment。

abstract.en: Imagine a joint that swings in every direction without breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个关节向各个方向自由转动，却始终不折断。

examples.en: The doctor played a pivotal role in controlling the outbreak.
examples.cn: 这位医生在控制疫情方面起了关键作用。

examples.en: That year was pivotal for the whole industry.
examples.cn: 那一年对整个行业来说都是关键的。

examples.en: The telescope is mounted on a pivotal arm so it can be turned easily.
examples.cn: 望远镜装在一个可转动的支臂上，方便转向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「批涡头」——一扇门靠销轴转，轴一转，局面就跟着转：关键、枢纽

root: 古法语 pivot（铰链销轴、转轴）→ 英语 pivot（枢轴；转动）→ pivotal（枢轴的→关键的）；更早来源一般认为存疑，有说法认为与拉丁语 piva（管、钉）有关。核心义「一切绕着转动的那个支点」。

sensesIntro.en: Pivotal starts from the hinge pin, names the joint that turns on it, then the decisive importance of that point for later events, and finally the turning point in time.
sensesIntro.cn: pivotal 从铰链上的销轴出发，先指绕轴转动的关节，再指那个支点对后续事件的决定性，最后指时间上的转折点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy door that turns on a single small pin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇沉重的大门，全靠一根小销轴转动。

branches.en: The decisive branch: whatever the whole plan turns on is pivotal.
branches.cn: 决定性分支：整个计划绕之转动的东西就是 pivotal。

branches.en: The time branch: a pivotal moment is where events turn a new way.
branches.cn: 时间分支：pivotal moment 是事件转向新方向的那一刻。

branches.en: The mechanical branch: a pivotal joint turns freely, and it is also what holds the frame together.
branches.cn: 机械分支：pivotal 的关节能自由转动，同时又把整个框架连在一起。

branches.en: All three branches share one point on which everything else depends.
branches.cn: 三个分支共用同一个中心点：别的都取决于它。

branches.en: The concrete hinge and the turning moment are the same picture at different sizes.
branches.cn: 具体的铰链与转折时刻，是同一画面在不同尺度上的呈现。

intro.en: Pivotal is built on the noun pivot with the adjective ending -al, and it feeds back into the adverb pivotally.
intro.cn: pivotal 由名词 pivot 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，再派生出副词 pivotally。

latinIntro.en: Pivot came through Old French; a Latin link to piva is sometimes proposed but is not certain.
latinIntro.cn: pivot 经古法语进入英语；它与拉丁语 piva 的联系只是一种推测，并不确定。

items.example: Pivot is the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pivot 是整个词族的核心。

items.example: The suffix -al forms pivotal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 pivotal。

items.example: Pivotal describes a decisive point.
items.exampleCN: pivotal 描述决定性的那一点。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms pivotally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 pivotally。

items.example: Pivotally modifies a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: pivotally 修饰表示动作的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms pivotality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 pivotality。

items.example: Pivoted forms a participle from pivot.
items.exampleCN: pivoted 是 pivot 的分词形式。

items.meaning: to be decisive in a process
items.example: The phrase is the everyday home of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个搭配是这个形容词的日常归宿。

definition_zh: 灰泥；抹灰；石膏；膏药；创可贴；抹灰；大量张贴
definition_en: a soft material that sets hard and is used to cover walls or to make casts, and also a small cloth stuck on a cut, or to cover a surface with a thick layer
core_image: 抹刀挑起一团湿灰泥，往粗糙的墙上一按，墙面立刻平了
scene: 新砌的砖墙坑坑洼洼，工人在墙前支起一块木板，一勺一勺地把浆料涂上去。He spread the plaster evenly, let it dry, then painted over it.
sceneCN: 这里 plaster 是「灰泥、抹灰」（第 1 个义项：抹在墙上、干后变硬的湿软材料）；句意为他把灰泥均匀地抹开，等它干透，再刷上一层漆。那把抹刀挑起的湿团，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 灰泥；石膏；膏药；创可贴；石膏粉
抹灰；在……上大量张贴；使变得平滑

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「抹灰工」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「抹灰工程」
过去分词作形容词，义为「贴满的」；英国口语还指「烂醉的」
plaster 加 board 构成的复合词，义为「石膏板」

senses.title: Soft material spread over walls
senses.definition: a soft mixture that is spread over walls and ceilings and sets hard
senses.definitionCN: 抹在墙面和天花板上、干后变硬的湿软混合物
senses.example: The workers covered the brick with fresh plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在砖面上抹了一层新灰泥。
senses.why: The Greek source names a salve that is smeared on; the first English sense is exactly that, a thin layer smeared over a rough surface and left to dry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的希腊语源头指「涂抹上去的药膏」；英语最早的义项正是如此——在粗糙表面上抹开薄薄一层，任其干硬。

senses.title: The act of coating a surface
senses.definition: to cover a wall or other surface with plaster or with a thick layer of something
senses.definitionCN: 在墙面等表面上涂灰泥，或厚厚地涂上一层东西
senses.example: They plastered the ceiling before the painters arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工来之前，他们先把天花板抹了灰。
senses.why: Once the material had a name, the action of smearing it on took the same word, the way butter and to butter share a form.
senses.whyCN: 材料有了名字之后，涂抹它的动作就用了同一个词，就像 butter 与 to butter 共用一个形式。

senses.title: A sticky dressing for a cut
senses.definition: a small piece of cloth or plastic with adhesive, stuck over a cut or small wound
senses.definitionCN: 一小块带黏性的布或塑料，贴在伤口上
senses.example: She put a plaster on his scraped knee and sent him back out to play.
senses.exampleCN: 她给男孩的膝盖贴上创可贴，让他又出去玩了。
senses.why: A dressing is again something smeared and stuck on the skin; British English keeps the old salve word here, while American English says band-aid.
senses.whyCN: 敷料同样是被涂抹并粘在皮肤上的东西；英式英语在这里保留了古老的「药膏」用法，美式英语则说 band-aid。

senses.title: The chalky substance for casts
senses.definition: a white powder made by heating gypsum, which sets hard when mixed with water
senses.definitionCN: 加热石膏矿得到的白色粉末，与水混合后会硬化
senses.example: The doctor set his arm in a tight plaster cast.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给他的手臂打上了绷得很紧的石膏。
senses.why: Plaster of Paris was named after the gypsum beds of Montmartre; the powder hardens like wall coating, so it took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 「巴黎石膏」因蒙马特的石膏矿得名；这种粉末像墙面涂料一样会硬化，于是共用了 plaster 这个名字。

senses.title: Covering with things or words
senses.definition: to cover a surface thickly with notices, pictures or information, often messily
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上厚厚地贴满告示、图片或信息，常常显得凌乱
senses.example: The whole wall was plastered with election posters.
senses.exampleCN: 整面墙上贴满了选举海报。
senses.why: Anything smeared on thickly, from posters to slogans and praise, repeats the picture of the trowel spreading a sticky layer over everything.
senses.whyCN: 凡是被厚厚糊上去的东西，从海报到口号再到赞美，都重复了抹刀把黏层铺满一切的画面。

intro.en: Plaster comes from Greek emplastron, a salve smeared on the skin, through Latin and Old English.
intro.cn: plaster 来自希腊语 emplastron（涂在皮肤上的药膏），经拉丁语与古英语进入现代英语。

items.en: Emplastron means something smeared on, from the verb emplassein, to plaster on.
items.cn: emplastron 意为「涂抹上去之物」，来自动词 emplassein（涂抹上去）。

items.en: Latin emplastrum keeps the word for a salve or poultice.
items.cn: 拉丁语 emplastrum 保留了「药膏、膏药」的意思。

items.en: The form plaster is recorded from about the tenth century for a medicinal salve.
items.cn: plaster 这个形式约在十世纪就以「药膏」之义被记录下来。

items.en: The word spread to wall coating: a layer smeared on and left to harden.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到墙面涂料：抹上一层，任其干硬。

items.en: Plaster of Paris gave the powder its name, after the gypsum quarried in Montmartre.
items.cn: 「巴黎石膏」因蒙马特开采的石膏矿而得名，这个名称被赋予这种粉末。

items.en: The verb followed the noun: first wall coating, then sticking things on, then the figurative sense of covering a person with praise or abuse.
items.cn: 动词跟随名词，从墙面涂层到贴物，再到用褒贬之词铺天盖地覆盖的比喻义。

note.en: The first group gathers the plaster family and look-alike words; the second gathers other wall finishes and dressings.
note.cn: 第一组收 plaster 词族与形近词；第二组收其他墙面涂层与敷料。

entries.definition: a person whose job is to cover walls with plaster
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抹灰工」，同一词根加 -er 构成

entries.definition: a rigid board of plaster between two layers of paper, used for walls
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石膏板」，由 plaster 与 board 合成的复合词

entries.definition: covered thickly with something, or, in British slang, very drunk
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贴满的」，英国俚语里还指「烂醉的」

entries.definition: decorative plaster shaping on ceilings and walls
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「石膏装饰」，指天花板与墙面上的石膏花纹

entries.definition: a fine plaster used on outside walls, often with a decorative finish
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灰墁、外墙饰面」，多用在外墙上

entries.definition: the lime and sand paste that joins bricks together
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砂浆」，用来把砖粘在一起

entries.definition: a strip of cloth wrapped round a wound, broader than a plaster
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绷带」，缠在伤口上的布条，范围比创可贴大

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek salve root, the real word family and the phrases plaster really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用希腊语「药膏」词根、真实的词族以及 plaster 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The Greek emplastron is a salve smeared on, so the wall coating and the sticky dressing are one idea.
normal.cn: 希腊语 emplastron 是涂抹上去的药膏，所以墙面涂料与黏性敷料本是同一个想法。

normal.en: Plaster of Paris takes its name from the gypsum quarried near Montmartre in Paris.
normal.cn: plaster of Paris 得名于巴黎蒙马特附近开采的石膏。

normal.en: A plaster cast holds a broken bone the way a coat of plaster holds a wall.
normal.cn: plaster cast 固定断骨，就像一层灰泥固定一面墙。

normal.en: To be plastered with posters is to have the walls smeared full of them.
normal.cn: be plastered with posters 就是墙上被贴得满满当当。

normal.en: Plasterer and plastering are one letter apart: the worker and the work.
normal.cn: plasterer 与 plastering 只差一个字母：一个是工人，一个是活儿。

abstract.en: Picture a trowel lifting a grey lump and pressing it flat against a rough brick face.
abstract.cn: 想象一把抹刀挑起一团灰色浆料，压平在粗糙的砖面上。

abstract.en: Watch a hand smoothing layer after layer until the wall is perfectly level.
abstract.cn: 看着一只手一层又一层地抹平，直到墙面彻底平整。

abstract.en: See a single poster go up, then another, until the wall disappears under paper.
abstract.cn: 看一张海报贴上去，又一张，直到墙面消失在纸片之下。

examples.en: The plaster on the old ceiling was cracking.
examples.cn: 老天花板上的灰泥正在开裂。

examples.en: He plastered the wall with posters before the rally.
examples.cn: 集会之前，他把海报贴满了墙面。

examples.en: She fell off her bike and asked for a plaster.
examples.cn: 她从自行车上摔下来，要了一块创可贴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼拉丝」——把浆料泼上去、拉出一道道丝，再抹平墙面：灰泥

root: 希腊语 emplassein（涂抹上去）→ emplastron（药膏）→ 拉丁语 emplastrum → 古英语 plaster（药膏）→ 中古英语墙面涂料；核心义「抹上去、干后成形的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Plaster begins with a salve smeared on the skin, moves to the coating smeared on a wall, then to the act, the sticky dressing, the gypsum powder and finally to anything spread thickly.
sensesIntro.cn: plaster 从抹在皮肤上的药膏出发，转到抹在墙上的涂层，再分为涂抹的动作、黏性敷料、石膏粉，最后泛指一切厚厚涂上去的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trowel presses a wet grey lump flat against a rough wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：抹刀把一团湿灰泥压平在粗糙的墙上。

branches.en: The material branch: the wet layer that sets hard on the wall.
branches.cn: 材料分支：在墙上干硬的那一层湿涂料。

branches.en: The action branch: the verb names putting the layer on.
branches.cn: 动作分支：动词指把这一层涂上去的动作。

branches.en: The skin branch: the old salve survives as a small sticky patch.
branches.cn: 皮肤分支：古老的药膏以小小的黏性敷料延续下来。

branches.en: The solid branch: the same powder becomes a rigid cast.
branches.cn: 硬化分支：同一种粉末变成坚硬的石膏。

branches.en: The spreading branch: posters and slogans are thick layers hung on a wall.
branches.cn: 铺满分支：海报与口号是挂在墙上的厚层。

intro.en: Plaster is a whole borrowing from Greek, with the English family plasterer, plastering, plasterboard and plasterwork built around it.
intro.cn: plaster 是从希腊语整体借入的词，英语围绕它构成 plasterer、plastering、plasterboard 与 plasterwork。

latinIntro.en: Latin emplastrum is the path the Greek word took before it reached English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 emplastrum 是这个希腊词抵达英语之前所走的路径。

items.example: Plaster is the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: plaster 是整个词族的核心。

items.example: The suffix -er forms plasterer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 plasterer。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms plastering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 plastering。

items.example: The ending -ed forms plastered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 plastered。

items.example: Board joins plaster to form plasterboard.
items.exampleCN: board 与 plaster 合成 plasterboard。

items.example: Work joins plaster to form plasterwork.
items.exampleCN: work 与 plaster 合成 plasterwork。

items.example: The phrase names the hardening powder.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语指会硬化的石膏粉。

items.meaning: a hard support round a limb
items.example: The compound names the medical cast.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指医疗用的石膏。

items.example: Plastered describes a covered wall.
items.exampleCN: plastered 描述被覆盖的墙面。

definition_zh: 石膏板；纸面石膏板；整块的石膏板
definition_en: a rigid building panel of plaster pressed between two sheets of paper, used to line walls and ceilings, and by extension a sheet of this material
core_image: 两块硬纸板夹着一层石膏，像一块夹心纸板，立起来就是一面隔墙
scene: 木架搭好以后，工人把一块块沉重的硬板贴上去，墙面马上变得平整。They fixed the plasterboard to the frame with screws and then taped the joints.
sceneCN: 这里 plasterboard 是「石膏板」（第 1 个义项：夹着石膏、用来贴墙面的硬纸板）；句意为他们用螺丝把石膏板固定到骨架上，然后用胶带把接缝处理掉。两块纸板中间夹一层灰白的石膏，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 石膏板；纸面石膏板

derivatives.zh: 复合词前半部分，义为「灰泥；石膏」，也是「涂抹」的动词
复合词后半部分，义为「板、板材」
与 plasterboard 共享 plaster 一词，义为「抹灰」；石膏板正是替代抹灰的材料
同族词，义为「抹灰工」；装石膏板的板工和抹灰工常在同一工地作业

senses.title: The plaster and paper panel
senses.definition: a board of set plaster sandwiched between two layers of strong paper, used for the inner lining of walls and ceilings
senses.definitionCN: 石膏夹在两层坚韧纸张之间的板材，用于墙体和天花板的内部面层
senses.example: Plasterboard is much faster to fit than wet plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 装石膏板比抹湿灰泥快得多。
senses.why: The compound puts together the plaster that once had to be smeared on wet and the board that can be lifted up and screwed on dry.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把两件事拼在一起：过去必须湿着抹上去的 plaster，以及能直接抬起来用螺丝装上的 board。

senses.title: A single sheet of the material
senses.definition: one manufactured panel of this material, bought and carried as a separate unit
senses.definitionCN: 这块材料制成的一块板材，作为一个独立单位购买和搬运
senses.example: They carried twenty plasterboards up the stairs before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭前他们把二十块石膏板搬上了楼。
senses.why: Building material names easily shift from the substance to the counted unit, so plasterboard can also mean one sheet of it on a lorry.
senses.whyCN: 建材名称很容易从材质滑向可计数的单位，所以 plasterboard 也能指卡车上的一块板。

intro.en: Plasterboard is a modern compound of plaster and board, and it names an American invention of the final years of the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: plasterboard 是 plaster 与 board 构成的现代复合词，指的是十九世纪末美国发明的板材。

items.en: The first half goes back to Greek emplastron, a salve smeared on.
items.cn: 前半部分可追溯到希腊语 emplastron（涂抹上去的药膏）。

items.en: Plaster of Paris had long let builders cast and smooth surfaces, but always as a wet job.
items.cn: 巴黎石膏早就让工匠能浇铸和平整表面，但一直得湿着施工。

items.en: In the United States, panels of gypsum plaster between paper layers were produced in the last years of the century.
items.cn: 在美国，纸层夹石膏的板材在十九世纪末被生产出来。

items.en: The compound plasterboard named the dry way to finish a wall, and the material spread through building sites.
items.cn: 复合词 plasterboard 命名了完成墙面的「干法」，材料很快传遍工地。

items.en: Regional names grew beside it: plasterboard, drywall and gypsum board, with different habits in each country.
items.cn: 各地又长出不同的叫法：plasterboard、drywall 与 gypsum board，每个国家的习惯用法不同。

note.en: The first group gathers the two halves of the compound and other board words; the second gathers the wall lining materials it competes with.
note.cn: 第一组收这个复合词的两个词根与其它板材词；第二组收它在墙面上要与之一较高下的材料。

entries.definition: the American name for plasterboard, built on the idea of finishing a wall dry
entries.definitionCN: 名词，plasterboard 的美式叫法，字面是「干墙」，强调不湿着施工

entries.definition: a long flat piece of hard material, the second half of the compound
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「板、板材」，是复合词的后半部分

entries.definition: a thick piece of sawn timber; only the sound is close
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厚木板」；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: thin sheets of wood glued in layers and pressed into a board
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胶合板」，由多层木片胶合成板

entries.definition: a plaster finish put on outside walls
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灰墁」，用于外墙的石膏饰面

entries.definition: a cheap board made of wood chips glued together
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刨花板」，用木屑胶合而成的廉价板材

normalIntro.en: Plasterboard is a plain compound, and these hooks work through its two halves, its rivals and the jobs built round it.
normalIntro.cn: plasterboard 是一个直白的复合词，下面的钩子从它的两半、它的对手以及围绕它的工种入手。

normal.en: Plaster plus board: the plaster has already set, so this board comes on dry.
normal.cn: plaster 加 board：石膏早已在板里凝好，所以这块板是干着上的。

normal.en: The American word for the same thing is drywall, and the two names tell the same story.
normal.cn: 同一件东西的美式叫法是 drywall，两个名字讲的是同一个故事。

normal.en: Plasterboard replaced wet plaster in most new houses in the twentieth century.
normal.cn: 二十世纪里，plasterboard 在大多数新房中取代了湿抹灰。

normal.en: A plasterboard ceiling is often fixed to a metal frame rather than to timber.
normal.cn: plasterboard ceiling 常常固定在金属龙骨上，而不是木架上。

normal.en: Compare the family: plaster, plasterer, plastering and plasterboard differ only in their endings.
normal.cn: 对比这一家：plaster、plasterer、plastering 与 plasterboard 的区别只在词尾。

abstract.en: See two sheets of paper with a thick grey filling pressed between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两张纸中间被压进一层厚厚的灰色夹心。

abstract.en: Picture a worker lifting one heavy sheet alone and edge-walking it through a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工人独自抬起一整块沉重的板材，侧着身子挤过门口。

abstract.en: Imagine an empty room growing four smooth white walls in a single afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空房间在一个下午里长出四面光滑的白墙。

examples.en: We used plasterboard to line the inside of the roof.
examples.cn: 我们给屋顶的内侧装上了石膏板。

examples.en: The plasterboard covered the cable, so nobody knew where it went.
examples.cn: 石膏板把电缆挡住了，没人知道它通向哪里。

examples.en: Fix the plasterboard with long screws so it holds the weight.
examples.cn: 用长螺丝固定石膏板，这样它才承受得住重量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼拉丝板」——石膏夹在纸里，抹着拉出一层板：石膏板

root: plaster（希腊语 emplastron 药膏→灰泥、石膏）+ board（古英语 bord 板）＝石膏板；核心义「把灰泥预先压成一块干板」。

sensesIntro.en: Plasterboard has a substance sense, the paper-faced gypsum panel, and a countable sense, one such sheet on a site.
sensesIntro.cn: plasterboard 有材质义，即夹着石膏的纸面硬板；也有可数义，即工地上的一块板。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper over a thick grey filling, standing as a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张贴着厚灰色夹心的纸板，立起来就是一面墙。

branches.en: The material branch: the panel is named after what lies inside it.
branches.cn: 材料分支：板的名称来自板里的东西。

branches.en: The unit branch: the substance is counted sheet by sheet.
branches.cn: 单位分支：这种材料按块计数。

branches.en: The method branch: dry boards replace wet plaster, one panel at a time.
branches.cn: 方法分支：干板一块块取代了湿抹灰。

branches.en: The rival branch: drywall and gypsum board name the same thing in other places.
branches.cn: 对手分支：drywall 与 gypsum board 在别处指的是同一件东西。

branches.en: The finish branch: every sheet is taped and painted, so the board disappears behind a smooth surface.
branches.cn: 饰面分支：每一块都被贴胶带再刷漆，板就消失在平整的表面之后。

intro.en: Plasterboard is a native compound of two free words, plaster and board, and it joins the older plaster family.
intro.cn: plasterboard 是两个独立单词 plaster 与 board 构成的复合词，也属于较早的 plaster 词族。

latinIntro.en: Only the first half is Latin in origin, by way of Greek emplastron and Latin emplastrum.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前半部分有拉丁来源，经希腊语 emplastron 与拉丁语 emplastrum 传下来。

items.example: Plaster names the filling of the board.
items.exampleCN: plaster 点明板里的填充物。

items.example: Board names the shape of the panel.
items.exampleCN: board 点明板材的形状。

items.example: Plasterboard joins the two halves into one noun.
items.exampleCN: plasterboard 把两半合成一个名词。

items.example: The ending -ed forms plasterboarded.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 plasterboarded。

items.example: The -er ending forms plasterer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 plasterer。

items.example: The -ing ending forms plastering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 plastering。

items.example: Drywall puts the method into the name.
items.exampleCN: drywall 把施工方法写进了名字。

items.example: The phrase names the mineral inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语点明板里的矿物。

definition_zh: 似乎有理的；貌似可信的；能说会道的；看似真诚的
definition_en: seeming reasonable or probable, though not proven
core_image: 一位演讲者摊开双手，神情真诚，讲的故事听来处处说得通
scene: 会议上，一位顾问讲述了成本超支的原因，条条对得上，大家都点了头。At the meeting the consultant gave a plausible account of the cost overrun, and everyone nodded.
sceneCN: 这里 plausible 是「似乎有理的」（第 1 个义项：听起来合情合理）；句意：会上顾问对成本超支给了一个看似合理的说法，大家都点头了。

pos.zh: 似乎有理的；貌似可信的
能说会道的；花言巧语的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可信度；似乎有理」
加否定前缀 im- 构成，义为「难以置信的；说不通的」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「似乎有理地」
加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「可信性」，较少使用

senses.title: Seeming reasonable
senses.definition: sounding reasonable or likely to be true, without being proven
senses.definitionCN: 听起来合情合理或很可能是真的，但尚未得到证实
senses.example: She offered a plausible explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她对延误给出了一个说得通的解释。
senses.why: The Latin root plaudere means to clap, so a plausible idea is one that wins applause and seems sound to listeners.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 plaudere 意为「拍手」，所以听起来站得住的想法就像赢得掌声，让人觉得合理。

senses.title: Believable but unproven
senses.definition: convincing enough to be believed, though it may still be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 足以让人相信，但仍可能并不正确
senses.example: The theory is plausible but lacks evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论看起来可信，但缺少证据。
senses.why: The word keeps a shadow of doubt: seeming reasonable is not the same as being proved.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终带着一丝怀疑：「听起来合理」并不等于「已被证明」。

senses.title: Smooth and persuasive in speech
senses.definition: skilled at seeming right or sincere when speaking, often to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 说话时很会让话显得正确或真诚，往往带有欺瞒意味
senses.example: He is a plausible talker who charms his clients.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个能说会道的人，很能讨客户欢心。
senses.why: Since clapping comes from an audience, the word grew a sense of pleasing the listener rather than being true.
senses.whyCN: 既然掌声来自听众，这个词就生出「取悦听众而非属实」的含义。

senses.title: Acceptable to the ear or mind
senses.definition: acceptable or pleasing when heard or considered, as in music or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在听觉或思考上可以接受、顺耳悦心，多用于音乐或论证
senses.example: The melody is plausible to the ear, though hardly exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这段旋律听起来还算顺耳，只是谈不上精彩。
senses.why: Early use of the word described voices and music that pleased the ear, before it described reasons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词早期用来形容悦耳的声音与音乐，后来才用来形容理由。

intro.en: Plausible comes from Latin plausibilis, deserving applause, from plaudere, to clap.
intro.cn: plausible 来自拉丁语 plausibilis（值得鼓掌的），源于 plaudere（拍手）。

items.en: Plaudere means to clap or beat the hands.
items.cn: plaudere 意为拍手、拍掌。

items.en: Plausibilis means worthy of applause.
items.cn: plausibilis 意为值得鼓掌的。

items.en: Latin writers also apply it to speech that pleases the ear.
items.cn: 拉丁作家还用这个词形容悦耳的话语。

items.en: English adopts it as likely to win approval or belief.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示「容易赢得赞同或相信」。

items.en: Today it chiefly means sounding reasonable rather than certain.
items.cn: 今天它主要指听起来合理，而非确定为真。

note.en: Plausible shares the applause root with applaud and plausibility, and sits close to words for believable and likely.
note.cn: plausible 与 applaud、plausibility 共享「鼓掌」词根，并与表示「可信」「可能」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to clap in approval
entries.definitionCN: 鼓掌称赞，与 plausible 共享「拍手」词根

entries.definition: an expression of praise
entries.definitionCN: 喝彩；赞许

entries.definition: the quality of seeming reasonable
entries.definitionCN: 可信度；似乎有理

entries.definition: able to be believed
entries.definitionCN: 可信的，强调有证据支撑

entries.definition: easy to believe
entries.definitionCN: 可信的；让人容易相信的

entries.definition: likely to be true or happen
entries.definitionCN: 很可能的

normalIntro.en: Plausible is about what makes an audience nod or clap: it sounds right.
normalIntro.cn: plausible 讲的是让听众点头或鼓掌的东西：它听起来是对的。

normal.en: A plausible explanation is one that seems to fit the facts.
normal.cn: a plausible explanation 指看上去与事实相符的解释。

normal.en: Plausible carries doubt: plausible is not the same as true.
normal.cn: plausible 暗含疑点：貌似合理不等于真实。

normal.en: Compare implausible, the same word with im- added.
normal.cn: 对比 implausible，同一个词前加 im- 表示否定。

normal.en: A plausible speaker sounds sincere without proof.
normal.cn: a plausible speaker 指没有证据却让人觉得真诚的人。

normal.en: Plausible deniability lets a leader deny knowing.
normal.cn: plausible deniability 指让领导人可以推说并不知情。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker opening both hands as if offering the truth.
abstract.cn: 想象一位演讲者摊开双手，像是要把真相交给你。

abstract.en: Think of a smooth answer that solves the question but hides the flaw.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆滑的答案，解开了疑问却藏起了破绽。

abstract.en: See a polished sales pitch that everyone believes for one evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一段打磨过的说辞，让所有人都相信了一个晚上。

examples.en: The police found the witness account plausible but unproven.
examples.cn: 警方觉得证人的说法有道理，但尚未得到证实。

examples.en: There is no plausible reason for the sudden change of plan.
examples.cn: 对计划的突然改变，找不到任何说得通的理由。

examples.en: His plausible manner hid a complete lack of expertise.
examples.cn: 他那套能说会道的样子，掩盖了他毫无专业能力的事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普劳泽」——普通听众在下面「劳」心地点头称赞；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 plaudere（拍手）→ plausibilis（值得鼓掌的）→ 英语 plausible，核心义「听起来能赢得掌声，也就显得可信」。

sensesIntro.en: Plausible starts as sounding reasonable, adds the quiet doubt of being unproven, and then shifts to people who talk smoothly.
sensesIntro.cn: plausible 先指听起来有理，再加上「未被证实」的隐含疑点，最后引申到说话圆滑的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speech that wins applause and sounds right.
core.cn: 核心意象：赢得掌声、听起来站得住的话。

branches.en: Seeming reasonable is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 似乎有理是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Believable but unproven is the cautious sense.
branches.cn: 貌似可信而未证实是带谨慎色彩的义项。

branches.en: A plausible talker is the human sense.
branches.cn: 能说会道的人是人物义项。

branches.en: A plausible reason seems true precisely because it lacks proof.
branches.cn: 说得通的理由之所以像真的，正因为它还没被证明。

branches.en: Pleasing speech and pleasing music share the ear.
branches.cn: 悦耳的话与悦耳的音乐都关乎耳朵。

intro.en: Plausible is built on the Latin applause root plaud-, with English related words such as applaud and plausibility.
intro.cn: plausible 建立在拉丁语「鼓掌」词根 plaud- 之上，英语中还有 applaud、plausibility 等相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plaudere means to clap, plausibilis means worthy of applause, and the suffix -ible marks something that can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plaudere 意为拍手，plausibilis 意为值得鼓掌的，后缀 -ible 表示「可以……的」。

items.example: The root plaud- gives the applause image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 plaud- 提供鼓掌的意象。

items.example: Plausibilis is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: plausibilis 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms plaus-ible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 plaus-ible。

items.example: Applaud keeps the clapping action.
items.exampleCN: applaud 保留拍手的动作。

items.example: Applause shares the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: applause 来自同一个拉丁语动词。

items.example: Plaudit is praise voiced aloud.
items.exampleCN: plaudit 是大声表达的赞许。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms plausibility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 plausibility。

items.example: The prefix im- forms implausible.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 implausible。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms plausibly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 plausibly。

latinEntries.meaning: to clap, to beat the hands

definition_zh: 爱玩的；活泼有趣的；开玩笑的；调皮的；随意而为的
definition_en: full of fun and eager to play
core_image: 一只小狗叼着球，尾巴摇个不停，等你跟它玩
scene: 花园里，小狗叼着球在草地上打滚，尾巴摇得像风车一样。In the garden the puppy rolled on the grass, wearing a rather playful look.
sceneCN: 这里 playful 是「爱玩的、活泼的」（第 1 个义项：天生爱玩闹）；句意：花园里，小狗在草地上打滚，露出一副很想玩闹的样子。

pos.zh: 爱玩的；嬉戏的
开玩笑的；调皮的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「爱玩；顽皮」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「开玩笑地；顽皮地」
由 play 加 fellow 复合构成，义为「玩伴」，为较早的复合词
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不爱玩的；一本正经的」

senses.title: Eager to play
senses.definition: full of fun and fond of games or physical play
senses.definitionCN: 充满乐趣、喜欢游戏或身体活动的
senses.example: The playful puppy chased the ball all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这只爱玩的小狗追了一下午的球。
senses.why: The Old English root plegan means to move quickly and amuse oneself, so playful keeps a body in motion.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词根 plegan 意为快速活动、自得其乐，所以 playful 始终带着身体在动的画面。

senses.title: Joking rather than serious
senses.definition: said or done in fun, not as a serious statement
senses.definitionCN: 以玩笑方式说出或做出，并非严肃表态
senses.example: He made a playful remark about her new hat.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的新帽子打趣了一句。
senses.why: The word spreads from games to speech, where a remark is playful when it is not meant in earnest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从游戏扩展到言语：当一句话并非当真时，它就是 playful 的。

senses.title: Light and mischievous
senses.definition: lightly naughty, teasing or full of clever mischief
senses.definitionCN: 带着轻微淘气、逗弄或机灵的调皮
senses.example: She gave him a playful push and laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 她调皮地推了他一下，笑了。
senses.why: Play without harm becomes teasing, so playful carries a hint of naughtiness, never real anger.
senses.whyCN: 没有恶意的玩耍变成逗弄，于是 playful 带上一丝淘气，但从不真的生气。

senses.title: Free and imaginative in design
senses.titleCN: 随意而为的；富有想象力的
senses.definition: used of art, design or style that is free, lively and not strictly formal
senses.definitionCN: 形容艺术、设计或风格自由活泼，不拘一格
senses.example: The poster uses a playful mix of colours and shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 这张海报用色与造型都很俏皮。
senses.why: Because play has no fixed rule, the word also describes work that takes liberties for fun.
senses.whyCN: 因为玩耍本无固定规则，这个词也用来形容为求趣味而不拘一格的作品。

intro.en: Playful is English play plus the suffix -ful, and play goes back to Old English plegan.
intro.cn: playful 是英语 play 加后缀 -ful 构成，而 play 可追溯到古英语 plegan。

items.en: Plegan means to move quickly, amuse oneself or practise.
items.cn: plegan 意为快速活动、娱乐或练习。

items.en: Plaien covers games, music and childish sport.
items.cn: plaien 涵盖游戏、音乐与儿童玩乐。

items.en: Playful and playfully appear, formed with -ful and -ly.
items.cn: playful 与 playfully 出现，分别由 -ful 与 -ly 构成。

items.en: The word extends to playful wit and teasing remarks.
items.cn: 该词扩展到俏皮的才智与打趣的话语。

items.en: It now also names light-handed design and style.
items.cn: 如今它也用来形容轻松灵动的设计与风格。

note.en: Playful is built from play and -ful, and sits near words for fun, mischief and light-hearted life.
note.cn: playful 由 play 加 -ful 构成，与表示「好玩」「顽皮」「轻松」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to take part in a game
entries.definitionCN: 玩；游戏，是 playful 的基础词

entries.definition: the quality of being fond of fun
entries.definitionCN: 爱玩；顽皮

entries.definition: in a joking or cheerful way
entries.definitionCN: 开玩笑地；顽皮地

entries.definition: naughtily playful or teasing
entries.definitionCN: 顽皮的；爱捣乱的，比 playful 更强调淘气

entries.definition: full of high spirits and play
entries.definitionCN: 嬉闹的；欢腾的

entries.definition: cheerful and free from worry
entries.definitionCN: 轻松的；无忧无虑的

normalIntro.en: Playful is simply play plus -ful, so it names someone or something filled with play.
normalIntro.cn: playful 就是 play 加 -ful，表示「充满玩的」，所以指人或事物满身是玩的劲头。

normal.en: The suffix -ful means full of, so playful means full of play.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为「充满」，所以 playful 就是充满玩闹的。

normal.en: A playful tone keeps a joke from sounding angry.
normal.cn: a playful tone 让玩笑听起来不带怒气。

normal.en: Playful banter is friendly teasing.
normal.cn: playful banter 指友好的互相打趣。

normal.en: Compare playfulness and playfully, the noun and adverb forms.
normal.cn: 对比 playfulness 与 playfully，分别是名词与副词形式。

normal.en: A playful design breaks strict rules with a smile.
normal.cn: a playful design 带着笑意打破严格规则。

abstract.en: Picture a puppy in a garden, ready to run after any ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小狗在花园里，随时准备去追任何一只球。

abstract.en: Imagine a friend winking right after a joke.
abstract.cn: 想象朋友说完笑话后眨了一下眼。

abstract.en: Think of a child tapping a favourite toy and giggling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子敲敲最爱的玩具，咯咯直笑。

examples.en: Her tone stayed playful even while giving advice.
examples.cn: 即使给建议时，她的语气也依然是玩笑式的。

examples.en: The children kept a playful spirit during the long journey.
examples.cn: 漫长的旅途中，孩子们一直保持爱玩闹的劲头。

examples.en: The lettering on the cover is playful and full of curves.
examples.cn: 封面上的字体随意俏皮，满是曲线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑雷福」——一边「扑」倒一边打「雷」都不怕，纯粹是玩闹的福气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 plegan（快速活动；自娱）→ 中古英语 plaien（游戏）→ play（玩）+ 后缀 -ful（充满）→ playful，核心义「满身是玩的劲」。

sensesIntro.en: Playful first describes bodies at play, then speech in fun, then light mischief, and finally free design.
sensesIntro.cn: playful 先形容玩闹的身体，再形容开玩笑的话，接着形容无伤大雅的淘气，最后形容自由随性的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tail wagging, ready for a game.
core.cn: 核心意象：尾巴摇个不停，等着一起玩。

branches.en: Being eager to play is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 爱玩是身体层面的义项。

branches.en: Joking speech is the verbal sense.
branches.cn: 玩笑话是言语层面的义项。

branches.en: Light mischief is the teasing sense.
branches.cn: 轻微淘气是逗弄性质的义项。

branches.en: Both a game and a cheeky push share friendly play.
branches.cn: 游戏与调皮的推搡都出于友好的玩乐之心。

branches.en: A joke and a playful design both break the serious rule.
branches.cn: 玩笑与俏皮设计都是对严肃规则的轻松突破。

intro.en: Playful is English play with the adjective suffix -ful, a pattern seen in joyful, careful and helpful.
intro.cn: playful 是英语 play 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，joyful、careful、helpful 都是同一构词法。

latinIntro.en: The base play is Old English, not Latin; -ful comes from Old English full, and only Latin spelling forms are noted here.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 play 出自古英语，并非拉丁语；-ful 源自古英语 full，这里只记录拉丁语拼写形态作为参照。

items.meaning: to move quickly, to amuse oneself
items.example: Plegan is the earliest recorded base.
items.exampleCN: plegan 是文献中最早的词形。

items.example: Play is the modern base word.
items.exampleCN: play 是现代基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms playful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 playful。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms playfulness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 playfulness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms playfully.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 playfully。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unplayful.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unplayful。

items.example: Playmate joins play with mate.
items.exampleCN: playmate 由 play 与 mate 合成。

items.example: Playful describes a cheerful nature.
items.exampleCN: playful 形容欢快的性格。

items.example: Plaything joins play with thing.
items.exampleCN: plaything 由 play 与 thing 合成。

definition_zh: 剧作家；编剧
definition_en: a person who writes plays for the theatre
core_image: 书桌前，一只手在稿纸上写下对白，旁边是排练厅的简易舞台
scene: 深夜的排练厅里，编剧还在灯下修改第三幕的对白。In the rehearsal room the playwright kept rewriting the dialogue of the third act.
sceneCN: 这里 playwright 是「剧作家」（第 1 个义项：写剧本的人）；句意：排练厅里，剧作家一直在重写第三幕的对白。

pos.zh: 剧作家；编剧

collocations.phrase: the playwright is a master of dialogue
collocations.zh: 剧作家是写对白的高手

derivatives.zh: 由 playwright 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「剧本创作」
由 screen 加 writer 复合构成，义为「电影编剧」，与戏剧剧作家相区分

senses.title: A writer of plays
senses.definition: a person who writes plays, especially for performance on stage
senses.definitionCN: 专门写剧本供舞台演出的人
senses.example: The playwright revised the ending five times.
senses.exampleCN: 这位剧作家把结尾改了五次。
senses.why: The second half -wright is an old word for a maker of things, so a playwright is literally a maker of plays.
senses.whyCN: 后半部分 -wright 是古语中「制造者」的词，所以 playwright 字面上就是「造戏的人」。

senses.title: A craftsperson of stage dialogue
senses.definition: one whose craft is shaping speeches, scenes and stage action for actors
senses.definitionCN: 以打磨台词、场次与舞台行动供演员使用为手艺的人
senses.example: As a playwright she is known for short, sharp speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 作为剧作家，她以短促犀利的台词著称。
senses.why: The maker sense in -wright turns writing into a craft, close to a wheelwright shaping a wheel.
senses.whyCN: -wright 的「制造者」含义把写作变成一门手艺，就像造车轮的匠人打磨轮子。

senses.title: Author credited at the first performance
senses.definition: the person named as the author of a play in the programme and the reviews
senses.definitionCN: 在节目单与剧评中被列为剧本作者的人
senses.example: The programme lists the playwright above the director.
senses.exampleCN: 节目单把剧作家排在导演前面。
senses.why: Theatre practice gives the script a single named author, so the word also names a role in a production.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧惯例会为剧本指定一位署名作者，因此这个词也指剧组中的一个角色。

senses.title: A maker of dramatic scenes
senses.definition: figuratively, anyone who arranges events like scenes in a drama
senses.definitionCN: 比喻意义上，像安排戏剧场面那样布置事件的人
senses.example: The politician was the playwright of his own downfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这位政治家是自己垮台的编剧。
senses.why: Because plays are built from arranged scenes, the word can stretch to anyone who stages real events.
senses.whyCN: 因为戏剧由安排好的场次构成，这个词就扩展到把现实事件编排成戏的人。

intro.en: Playwright joins play and wright, and wright goes back to Old English wryhta, a maker or worker in wood or metal.
intro.cn: playwright 由 play 与 wright 合成，wright 可追溯到古英语 wryhta，指木工或金属匠人。

items.en: Wryhta means a worker or maker, as in wainwright.
items.cn: wryhta 意为工匠、制造者，如 wainwright（造马车匠）。

items.en: Plegan means to move quickly and amuse oneself.
items.cn: plegan 意为快速活动、自娱自乐。

items.en: Play-wright and playwright name a maker of plays.
items.cn: play-wright 与 playwright 用来称呼写剧本的人。

items.en: The spelling shifts between play-wright and playwright.
items.cn: 这一时期的拼写游移于 play-wright 与 playwright 之间。

items.en: The spelling playwright is fixed, with the wright half no longer felt as a word.
items.cn: 现代英语固定写作 playwright，wright 这一半已不被视为独立词。

note.en: Playwright hides the old maker word wright inside it, and belongs to the world of drama and theatre crafts.
note.cn: playwright 内部藏着古语中表示「制造者」的 wright，属于戏剧与舞台工艺的世界。

entries.definition: a maker or builder of something
entries.definitionCN: 制造者；匠人，是 playwright 的后半部分

entries.definition: a builder of ships
entries.definitionCN: 造船匠，同用 -wright

entries.definition: a maker of wheels
entries.definitionCN: 造车轮的匠人

entries.definition: a writer of dramas
entries.definitionCN: 剧作家，是最直接的近义词

entries.definition: a writer of film scripts
entries.definitionCN: 电影编剧

entries.definition: a writer of opera texts
entries.definitionCN: 歌剧脚本作者

normalIntro.en: Playwright looks like play plus write, but its tail is the old maker word wright.
normalIntro.cn: playwright 看起来像 play 加 write，可它的后半截其实是老词 wright（制造者）。

normal.en: Remember the tail wright, as in shipwright and wheelwright, a maker.
normal.cn: 记住结尾 wright，就像 shipwright、wheelwright，意思是制造者。

normal.en: The spelling is playwright, not playwrite, so keep the w.
normal.cn: 拼写是 playwright 而不是 playwrite，要留住那个 w。

normal.en: Playwright pairs naturally with playwright and director, a common credit.
normal.cn: playwright 常与 director 并列出现在演职员表里。

normal.en: Compare playwright with dramatist, the plainer synonym.
normal.cn: 对比 dramatist，那是更朴素的同义词。

normal.en: Playwriting names the craft of the playwright.
normal.cn: playwriting 指剧作家的这门手艺。

abstract.en: See a maker shaping lines of dialogue as a craftsman shapes wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一位匠人把一句句台词像木头那样打磨成型。

abstract.en: Think of a rehearsal with the writer crossing out a whole act.
abstract.cn: 想象排练现场，作者把整整一幕划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a programme with the central name set in bold.
abstract.cn: 想象一张节目单，正中那个名字印得最粗。

examples.en: The festival invited playwrights from three countries.
examples.cn: 戏剧节邀请了来自三个国家的剧作家。

examples.en: A good playwright hears the actor while writing the line.
examples.cn: 好的剧作家写下台词时就能听见演员的声音。

examples.en: The director and the playwright argued about the final scene.
examples.cn: 导演与编剧为最后一场戏争执不下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来赖特」——剧本一「扑」上桌，就「赖」上这行当，成为特殊的手艺人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 wryhta（匠人、制造者）+ 中古英语 play（戏）→ playwright（造戏的人），与 shipwright、wheelwright 同用一个「工匠」词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Playwright means a maker of plays, then a craftsman of stage language, then a credited author, and finally anyone who stages events.
sensesIntro.cn: playwright 先指写戏的人，再指打磨舞台语言的手艺人，又指署名作者，最后引申为编排事件的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a maker who builds scenes out of words.
core.cn: 核心意象：用文字把场面搭建起来的人。

branches.en: A writer of plays is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 写剧本的人是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A crafter of dialogue is the craft sense.
branches.cn: 打磨台词的手艺人是手艺义项。

branches.en: The credited author is the theatre role sense.
branches.cn: 署名作者是戏剧体制中的角色义项。

branches.en: The writer and the credited name are usually the same person.
branches.cn: 写戏的人与节目单上的署名通常是同一个人。

branches.en: Both a playwright and a schemer arrange a scene.
branches.cn: 剧作家与幕后者都在安排场面。

intro.en: Playwright is an English compound whose second half, wright, is a maker word also seen in shipwright.
intro.cn: playwright 是英语复合词，后半段 wright 与 shipwright 同属表示「制造者」的老词。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root: wright is Old English, and play goes back to Old English plegan, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词根：wright 来自古英语，play 可追溯到古英语 plegan，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Plegan becomes modern play.
items.exampleCN: plegan 演变为现代英语 play。

items.example: Play supplies the first half.
items.exampleCN: play 提供前半部分。

items.example: Wryhta becomes wright in modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: wryhta 在现代拼写中变为 wright。

items.example: The suffix -wright also forms cartwright.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -wright 也构成 cartwright（造车匠）。

items.example: Shipwright shows the maker pattern.
items.exampleCN: shipwright 展示了「制作者」式构词。

items.example: Wheelwright shows the same tail.
items.exampleCN: wheelwright 同一词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms playwriting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 playwriting。

items.example: Playwriting names the trade.
items.exampleCN: playwriting 指这门行当。

items.example: Playwright combines both halves.
items.exampleCN: playwright 由前后两半合成。

definition_zh: 恳求；请求；抗辩；（法庭上的）申诉理由
definition_en: an urgent request for something, or a statement made by someone in a court of law
core_image: 一个人张开双手、低头向前恳求，把心里最急的话递到对方耳边
scene: 法庭休庭前，被告家属挤在走廊尽头。The lawyer made a final plea for more time to prepare the case.
sceneCN: 这里 plea 是「恳求、请求」（第 1 个义项：急切地请求某人给予某物或做某事）；句意为律师最后一次恳求多给一些准备案件的时间。

pos.zh: 恳求；请求；抗辩理由；申诉

derivatives.zh: 由同源动词构成，义为「恳求；辩护；答辩」
plead 加名词后缀构成，义为「恳求；诉状」
plead 加形容词后缀构成，义为「可辩护的；可申诉的」

senses.title: An urgent request
senses.definition: a serious and urgent request made to someone
senses.definitionCN: 向某人提出的郑重而急切的请求
senses.example: Her plea for help was finally answered.
senses.exampleCN: 她求助的恳求终于得到了回应。
senses.why: The Old French noun names a lawsuit or a request, so the core act is asking earnestly for something.
senses.whyCN: 古法语名词本指诉讼或请求，所以核心动作就是恳切地开口索要某物。

senses.title: A reason offered as a defence
senses.definition: a statement that someone offers to explain or excuse an action
senses.definitionCN: 为某行为作解释或开脱而给出的说法
senses.example: He ignored the letters with a plea of being too busy.
senses.exampleCN: 他以太忙为理由不理那些信件。
senses.why: The legal request turns inward: instead of asking for something, the speaker offers reasons to be excused.
senses.whyCN: 法律意义上的请求转向内里：说话人不再索取某物，而是提出理由为自己开脱。

senses.title: A formal answer in court
senses.definition: the answer that a defendant gives to a charge in a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 被告在法庭上针对指控给出的正式答复
senses.example: The accused entered a plea of not guilty.
senses.exampleCN: 被告作了无罪答辩。
senses.why: In court the earnest request hardens into a fixed formula: guilty or not guilty.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，恳切的请求固化成一句固定的答复：有罪或无罪。

senses.title: An emotional argument or appeal
senses.definition: a strong public appeal for people to act or to change
senses.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地呼吁人们行动或改变
senses.example: The charity issued a plea to reduce food waste.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构发出减少食物浪费的呼吁。
senses.why: The scale of the request widens from one listener to a public audience.
senses.whyCN: 请求的对象从一个人扩大到公众，恳求因而变成公开的呼吁。

senses.title: A desperate appeal for mercy
senses.definition: a tearful appeal to a judge or ruler to show kindness
senses.definitionCN: 含泪向法官或统治者乞求开恩
senses.example: The prisoner made one last plea for mercy.
senses.exampleCN: 囚犯最后乞求宽恕。
senses.why: When the fear of punishment is greatest, the request becomes an appeal for kindness.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧惩罚达到极点，请求就变成了对仁慈的乞求。

intro.en: Plea comes from Old French plai or plaid, a lawsuit or formal argument, from medieval Latin placitum, something pleasing or agreed, from Latin placere, to please.
intro.cn: plea 来自古法语 plai 或 plaid（诉讼、正式陈述），其源头是中世纪拉丁语 placitum（令人满意或经双方同意之事），再上溯到拉丁语 placere（使满意）。

items.en: Placere means to please or to be acceptable.
items.cn: placere 意为使满意、被接受。

items.en: Placitum names a decision or an agreement that pleases both sides.
items.cn: placitum 指令双方满意的一项决定或约定。

items.en: In legal use placitum comes to mean a formal case or argument.
items.cn: 在法律用法中，placitum 转指正式案件或陈词。

items.en: Plai or plaid means a lawsuit, an argument, or a request.
items.cn: plai 或 plaid 意为诉讼、争辩或请求。

items.en: Plea enters English as a legal term for a suit or an argument in court.
items.cn: plea 以法律术语进入英语，指诉讼或法庭上的争辩。

items.en: The word widens from the courtroom to any earnest request.
items.cn: 这个词从法庭扩展到任何恳切的请求。

note.en: Plea sits beside its own verb plead and other words of asking, such as request and appeal.
note.cn: plea 与同源动词 plead 相邻，也与 request、appeal 这类「请求」词相邻。

entries.definition: to ask earnestly or to argue a case
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；辩护

entries.definition: formal statements made in a lawsuit
entries.definitionCN: 诉状；诉讼文书

entries.definition: able to be argued in court
entries.definitionCN: 可辩护的

entries.definition: an urgent request for support
entries.definitionCN: 呼吁；恳求

entries.definition: a polite act of asking for something
entries.definitionCN: 请求；要求

entries.definition: a signed written request to an authority
entries.definitionCN: 请愿书；请愿

normalIntro.en: Plea and plead share one root: both are about opening the mouth to ask or to argue.
normalIntro.cn: plea 与 plead 同根：都指张口请求或争辩。

normal.en: Plead is the verb and plea is the noun of the same act.
normal.cn: plead 是这个动作的动词，plea 是名词。

normal.en: Make a plea means to issue an urgent request.
normal.cn: make a plea 意为发出急切请求。

normal.en: In court a defendant enters a plea of guilty or not guilty.
normal.cn: 在法庭上，被告要作有罪或无罪的答辩。

normal.en: A plea for mercy is the last request of a condemned prisoner.
normal.cn: plea for mercy 是死囚最后的请求。

normal.en: Compare request, which is neutral, while plea carries urgency and feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 request：request 中性，plea 带有急切与情感。

abstract.en: Picture two open palms held out toward a listener.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌摊开，伸向听者。

abstract.en: Imagine a small written excuse held up to explain a late arrival.
abstract.cn: 想象举着一张写着理由的小纸条，为迟到开脱。

abstract.en: Think of a defendant standing up to answer a single word: guilty.
abstract.cn: 想象被告站起来，只回答一个词：有罪。

examples.en: The villagers sent a plea for clean water.
examples.cn: 村民们发出了提供清洁用水的恳求。

examples.en: He was released on the plea that he had acted in self defence.
examples.cn: 他以正当防卫为由获得释放。

examples.en: The judge listened carefully to the plea of the young defendant.
examples.cn: 法官仔细听取了年轻被告的答辩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑咧」——扑倒在地、嘴里喊咧，就是恳求；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使满意）→ 中世纪拉丁语 placitum（令人满意的决定、约定）→ 古法语 plai / plaid（诉讼、请求）→ 英语 plea（抗辩；恳求）。

sensesIntro.en: Plea begins as the legal request or argument in court, then widens into any earnest request and finally into a public appeal.
sensesIntro.cn: plea 起于法庭上的请求与陈词，再扩大到任何恳切的请求，最后成为公开的呼吁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open palms held out while asking urgently.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开双手急切地开口请求。

branches.en: The everyday urgent request is the widest sense.
branches.cn: 日常的急切请求是范围最广的义项。

branches.en: Offering reasons to be excused is the defence sense.
branches.cn: 以理由开脱是抗辩义项。

branches.en: The formal court answer is the legal sense.
branches.cn: 正式的法庭答复是法律义项。

branches.en: A private plea can grow into a public appeal.
branches.cn: 私人的恳求可以发展为公开的呼吁。

branches.en: A defendant both answers a charge and asks for mercy.
branches.cn: 被告既要对指控作答，也会乞求宽恕。

intro.en: Plea is a noun of French and Latin origin, with plead and pleading built on the same stem.
intro.cn: plea 是源自古法语与拉丁语的名词，plead 与 pleading 构建在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin placere means to please, and medieval placitum names a decision that pleases both sides.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 placere 意为使满意，中世纪的 placitum 指令双方满意的一项决定。

items.example: Placere gives the root of the word.
items.exampleCN: placere 提供这个词的词根。

items.example: Placitum is a matter agreed by both sides.
items.exampleCN: placitum 指双方议定之事。

items.example: Plai carries the word into French law.
items.exampleCN: plai 把这个词带入法语法律。

items.example: Plea keeps the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: plea 保留了法律含义。

items.example: Plead is the matching verb.
items.exampleCN: plead 是对应的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms pleading.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 pleading。

items.example: The suffix -able forms pleadable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 pleadable。

items.example: Pleas takes a simple plural ending.
items.exampleCN: pleas 加简单复数词尾。

definition_zh: 全体的；全体出席的；完全的；无限制的
definition_en: attended by all who are entitled to attend, or complete and without limits
core_image: 一间大会议厅里座无虚席，所有本应到场的人全都坐在灯下
scene: 会期最后一天，代表们从各个分组讨论室回到主会场。The plenary session began with a report on the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 plenary 是「全体的、全体出席的」（第 1 个义项：所有应到成员都出席的）；句意为全体会议以一份预算报告开场。

pos.zh: 全体出席的；全体的；完全的；无限制的
全体会议

derivatives.zh: plenary 加副词后缀构成，义为「完全地；以全体形式」
由拉丁语 plenitudo 借入，与 plenary 同享「满」词根，义为「充实；充盈」
前缀 re-（再）与「满」词根结合构成，义为「补充；重新装满」

senses.title: Attended by all members
senses.definition: held with every person who has the right to attend present
senses.definitionCN: 所有有权出席的人都到场而举行的
senses.example: The committee closed with a plenary meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会以一场全体会议收尾。
senses.why: Latin plenus means full, so a plenary gathering is a hall filled with every member.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 plenus 意为「满」，所以全体出席的集会就是坐满了每一位成员的大厅。

senses.title: Complete and absolute
senses.definition: full and complete, with nothing left out
senses.definitionCN: 完整彻底，没有任何遗漏
senses.example: The scholar gave a plenary account of the topic.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者对该课题作了完整的阐述。
senses.why: From a full room the sense moves to a full amount or a full account.
senses.whyCN: 从「满座」的会场转向「满量」的论述，义项由空间转向程度。

senses.title: Unlimited in power
senses.definition: having full power to act without limits
senses.definitionCN: 拥有不受限制的完整权力
senses.example: The council holds plenary powers over the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会对该地区拥有全权。
senses.why: A full grant of authority leaves no part of the decision outside the holder.
senses.whyCN: 完整的授权意味着没有任何决策部分留在持有者之外。

senses.title: A full assembly of delegates
senses.definition: a session that all delegates attend together
senses.definitionCN: 全体代表共同出席的一场会议
senses.example: She spoke at the closing plenary in Geneva.
senses.exampleCN: 她在日内瓦的闭幕全体会议上发言。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun by naming the very meeting it describes.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接变成名词，所指正是它所描述的那场会议。

intro.en: Plenary comes from late Latin plenarius, complete, from Latin plenus, full, from the root ple-, to fill.
intro.cn: plenary 来自晚期拉丁语 plenarius（完整的），源于拉丁语 plenus（满的），再上溯到词根 ple-（充满）。

items.en: The reconstructed root ple- means to fill.
items.cn: 重构词根 ple- 意为充满。

items.en: Plenus means full, and plenarius means complete.
items.cn: plenus 意为满的，plenarius 意为完整的。

items.en: Legal and church Latin use plenarius for fully held bodies.
items.cn: 法律与教会拉丁语用 plenarius 指完整举行的集会。

items.en: Plenaire names a session with everyone present.
items.cn: plenaire 指所有人都到场的会议。

items.en: Plenary enters English as a church and legal term.
items.cn: plenary 在十六世纪以教会与法律术语进入英语。

items.en: Modern use spreads to conferences, courts and full authority.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到会议、法庭与全权。

note.en: Plenary belongs to the family of plenus, full, beside plenty, complete and replete.
note.cn: plenary 属于 plenus（满）一族，与 plenty、complete、replete 相邻。

entries.definition: a large amount
entries.definitionCN: 充足；大量

entries.definition: the state of being full
entries.definitionCN: 充满；充分

entries.definition: filled to the brim
entries.definitionCN: 充满的

entries.definition: containing everything possible
entries.definitionCN: 满的；完全的

entries.definition: having every part
entries.definitionCN: 完整的

entries.definition: unlimited in power
entries.definitionCN: 绝对的；无限制的

normalIntro.en: Plenary is built on the root plen-, full, so every sense carries a picture of fullness.
normalIntro.cn: plenary 建立在词根 plen-（满）之上，每个义项都带着「满」的画面。

normal.en: A plenary session is one where the whole house sits together.
normal.cn: plenary session 指全院坐在一起开会。

normal.en: Plenary powers are powers without any limit.
normal.cn: plenary powers 是不受任何限制的权力。

normal.en: The root plen- also builds plenty and plenitude.
normal.cn: 词根 plen- 还构成 plenty 与 plenitude。

normal.en: Latin plenus means full, so plenary began as a word for a full meeting.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plenus 意为满，plenary 最初指坐满人的会议。

normal.en: Compare total, which counts parts, while plenary stresses that everyone is present.
normal.cn: 对比 total：total 计数，plenary 强调所有人都到场。

abstract.en: Picture a vast hall where every chair is taken.
abstract.cn: 想象一间大厅里每个座位都坐了人。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup filled to the very top with no drop missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子倒得满满，一滴也不少。

abstract.en: Think of a single key that unlocks every door in the building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开整栋楼的每一扇门。

examples.en: The plenary debate lasted well past midnight.
examples.cn: 全体辩论一直持续到午夜以后。

examples.en: Delegates agreed to hold a plenary on the final morning.
examples.cn: 代表们同意在最后一天上午举行全体会议。

examples.en: The treaty gave plenary authority to the commission.
examples.cn: 该条约赋予委员会全权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺列呢」——把座位一排排铺满列好，人全都到齐，就是全体会议；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语重构词根 ple-（充满）→ 拉丁语 plenus（满的）、plenarius（完整的）→ 晚期拉丁语与中世纪法语 → 英语 plenary（全体出席的；完全的；全权的）。

sensesIntro.en: Plenary starts with a gathering where every seat is taken, grows into complete or absolute, and then names the full meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: plenary 起于「每席都有人」的集会，发展出「完全的、绝对的」，最后直接指「全体会议」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall where every seat is filled by the people entitled to be there.
core.cn: 核心意象：大厅里每个座位都坐着有权到场的成员。

branches.en: All members present is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 全体出席是第一个也最常见的义项。

branches.en: Fullness of parts becomes the sense of complete.
branches.cn: 各部分都齐就变成完整无缺的义项。

branches.en: A full grant of power is the legal and political sense.
branches.cn: 完整授权是法律与政治义项。

branches.en: The meeting itself is named by the same word.
branches.cn: 会议本身也用同一个词来命名。

branches.en: A plenary session often has plenary power to decide.
branches.cn: 全体会议往往拥有作决定的全权。

intro.en: Plenary is a learned Latin adjective, built on plenus, full, with a matching adverb and a fixed meeting phrase.
intro.cn: plenary 是学术性的拉丁语形容词，建立在 plenus（满）之上，并有对应的副词与固定会议说法。

latinIntro.en: Latin plenus means full, and plenarius means complete or total.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plenus 意为满的，plenarius 意为完整的、全部的。

items.example: The root ple- lies behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ple- 是这一词族的源头。

items.example: Plenus is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: plenus 是这个词的核心。

items.example: Plenarius is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: plenarius 是直接来源。

items.example: Plenary keeps the sense of fullness.
items.exampleCN: plenary 保留「满」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms plenarily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 plenarily。

items.example: Plenty shares the full root.
items.exampleCN: plenty 共享「满」的词根。

items.example: The suffix -tude forms plenitude.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tude 构成 plenitude。

items.example: The prefix re- joins a form of plere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 与 plere 的变形结合。

items.example: Plenaries takes a simple plural ending.
items.exampleCN: plenaries 加简单复数词尾。

definition_zh: 丰盛的；大量的；充分的；（古）慷慨的
definition_en: large in amount and freely given, usually used in a literary or old fashioned way
core_image: 谷仓门被推开，金黄的粮食堆到门口，几乎满溢出来
scene: 秋收后的农庄，粮囤一开就往外淌出麦粒。The old farmer pointed proudly at the plenteous harvest spread across the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 plenteous 是「丰盛的、大量的」（第 1 个义项：数量极多、供应充足）；句意为老农骄傲地指着铺满院子的丰收景象。

pos.zh: 丰盛的；大量的；充足的；（古）慷慨的

collocations.zh: 仁慈无尽（多见于经文用语）

derivatives.zh: plenteous 加副词后缀构成，义为「丰盛地；大量地」
plenteous 加名词后缀构成，义为「丰盛；充裕」
同源于拉丁语 plenus（满），义为「充足；大量」

senses.title: Existing in large amounts
senses.definition: present in large quantities, so that the supply seems endless
senses.definitionCN: 数量极多，供应看上去似乎没有穷尽
senses.example: The valley was rich with plenteous fruit and grain.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里结满了丰盛的果实与谷物。
senses.why: Latin plenus means full and plenty means fullness, so plenteous describes a supply filled to the brim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 plenus 意为「满」，plenty 意为「充足」，所以 plenteous 描述的是装满到桶沿的供应。

senses.title: More than enough for a need
senses.definition: enough to satisfy every need and still leave a surplus
senses.definitionCN: 足以满足一切需要而且仍有剩余
senses.example: Plenteous rain saved the crops in the dry summer.
senses.exampleCN: 充沛的雨水在干旱的夏天保住了庄稼。
senses.why: When the measure is a need, fullness becomes sufficiency rather than abundance.
senses.whyCN: 当衡量的对象是需要时，「满」就变成了「够用」，而不只是「多」。

senses.title: Freely generous
senses.definition: giving or showing kindness in a lavish and open way
senses.definitionCN: 大方地给予或展示善意
senses.example: The baron was plenteous in his gifts to the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 男爵对穷人的施予十分慷慨。
senses.why: A full hand that keeps giving turns abundance into generosity of character.
senses.whyCN: 一只装满并不断施予的手，把富足转成了性格上的慷慨。

senses.title: Literary or archaic register
senses.definition: a formal and old fashioned word, often kept today in poetry and scripture
senses.definitionCN: 正式而古旧的词，如今多留存于诗歌与经文中
senses.example: The hymn praises a plenteous redemption for all.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗颂扬为所有人预备的丰盛救赎。
senses.why: The heavy -eous ending belongs to an earlier style, so the word survives as a solemn echo.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的 -eous 词尾属于更早的文体，所以这个词以庄重的回响保存至今。

intro.en: Plenteous and plenty come from Latin plenus, full, through Old French plente, whose -ous was joined in English by analogy with words such as bounty.
intro.cn: plenteous 与 plenty 同源于拉丁语 plenus（满的），经古法语 plente 而来；英语中类比 bounty 这类词加上 -ous 词尾。

items.en: The reconstructed root ple- means to fill.
items.cn: 重构词根 ple- 意为充满。

items.en: Plenus means full, and plenitas means fullness.
items.cn: plenus 意为满的，plenitas 意为充满。

items.en: Plente carries the idea of plenty into French.
items.cn: plente 把充足的概念带入法语。

items.en: Plentevous appears, meaning abundant or generous.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 plentevous，意为丰足的、慷慨的。

items.en: Plenteous enters the Bible and the poets as a solemn word for abundance.
items.cn: plenteous 作为表示丰盛的庄重词进入圣经与诗作。

items.en: Plenty becomes the everyday noun while plenteous stays literary.
items.cn: plenty 成为日常名词，plenteous 则保持文学色彩。

note.en: Plenteous shares the root of plenty and sits beside abundant and ample as a literary cousin.
note.cn: plenteous 与 plenty 同根，并与 abundant、ample 这样表示充足的词相邻，是其中的文学表亲。

entries.definition: a large or sufficient amount
entries.definitionCN: 充足；大量

entries.definition: existing in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；丰富的

entries.definition: the state of being full
entries.definitionCN: 充实；丰盈

entries.definition: existing in very large quantities
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；丰富的

entries.definition: more than enough
entries.definitionCN: 充足的；充裕的

entries.definition: produced or supplied in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；丰沛的

normalIntro.en: Plenteous is the literary adjective of plenty, both built on the Latin word for full.
normalIntro.cn: plenteous 是 plenty 的文学形容词形式，二者都建立在拉丁语「满」这个词上。

normal.en: Plenteous takes the stem of plenty and an old -ous ending.
normal.cn: plenteous 由 plenty 的词干加古老的 -ous 词尾构成。

normal.en: A plenteous harvest fills the barn to the roof.
normal.cn: plenteous harvest 指把谷仓堆到屋顶的丰收。

normal.en: Plenteous rain means more rain than the fields need.
normal.cn: plenteous rain 指超出田地所需的雨水。

normal.en: Plenteous is mostly literary, while plentiful is the neutral choice.
normal.cn: plenteous 多用于文学，plentiful 才是中性的选项。

normal.en: The adverb plenteously and the noun plenteousness keep the same fullness.
normal.cn: 副词 plenteously 与名词 plenteousness 延续同样的「满」。

abstract.en: Picture a barn door pushed open onto a mountain of golden grain.
abstract.cn: 想象谷仓门被推开，里面是金黄色的粮山。

abstract.en: Imagine a well so full that the bucket overflows on the way up.
abstract.cn: 想象水井满得水桶提上来时一路外溢。

abstract.en: Think of a rich host filling every plate at the table a second time.
abstract.cn: 想象好客的主人为桌上每只盘子又添了一次菜。

examples.en: They thanked the gods for the plenteous fields.
examples.cn: 他们为丰饶的田地感谢神明。

examples.en: A plenteous supply of wood kept the house warm all winter.
examples.cn: 充足的木柴让屋子整个冬天都暖和。

examples.en: The poet praised a plenteous harvest under a wide sky.
examples.cn: 诗人赞美广阔天空下的丰盛收获。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普连特斯」——普天之下连着特多东西，多得满出来，就是丰盛；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语重构词根 ple-（充满）→ 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ 古法语 plente（充足）→ 中古英语 plentevous → 现代英语 plenteous（丰盛的；古）慷慨的。

sensesIntro.en: Plenteous moves from raw abundance to sufficiency, to generosity of giving, and finally to its old literary tone.
sensesIntro.cn: plenteous 从「多」走向「够」，再走向「慷慨地给」，最后落到古雅的文学色彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a barn door opening on grain heaped to the doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷仓门一开，粮食堆到门口。

branches.en: Large quantity is the plain sense of the word.
branches.cn: 数量多是这个词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: Sufficiency measures fullness against a need.
branches.cn: 充足义把「满」与具体需要相比较。

branches.en: Generosity turns fullness of goods into openness of heart.
branches.cn: 慷慨义把物品之满转为心胸之宽阔。

branches.en: The old ending marks the word as literary today.
branches.cn: 古老的词尾使这个词如今带有文学色彩。

branches.en: Plenteous store and plenteous giving share one root.
branches.cn: 丰盛的储备与丰盛的施予同出一根。

intro.en: Plenteous joins the Latin root for full to an English -ous ending, beside plenty, plentiful and plenitude.
intro.cn: plenteous 把表示「满」的拉丁词根接到英语 -ous 词尾上，与 plenty、plentiful、plenitude 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin plenus means full and plenitas means fullness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plenus 意为满的，plenitas 意为充满。

items.example: The root ple- underlies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ple- 支撑整个词族。

items.example: Plenus gives the root of the word.
items.exampleCN: plenus 给出这个词的词根。

items.example: Plenitas feeds the noun forms.
items.exampleCN: plenitas 滋养了名词形式。

items.example: Plente carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: plente 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms plenteous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 plenteous。

items.example: Plenty is the everyday cousin.
items.exampleCN: plenty 是日常使用的表亲词。

items.example: Plentiful is the neutral adjective.
items.exampleCN: plentiful 是中性的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms plenteously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 plenteously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms plenteousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 plenteousness。

definition_zh: 过多；过剩；大量
definition_en: a much larger amount of something than is needed or wanted
core_image: 盘子堆得高过杯沿，再也装不下一口
scene: 会议室里方案堆了一桌，人却还没定下做哪一个。The team gathered a plethora of plans but could not agree on one.
sceneCN: 这里 plethora 是「过多、过剩」（第 1 个义项：某物多得超出需要）；句意：团队收集了一大堆方案，却无法决定采用哪一个。

pos.zh: 过多；过剩；大量（常带「多得过分」的意味）

collocations.zh: 多得让人眼花缭乱的选择
大量的证据（常隐含「多到难辨真伪」）
富足与过剩（对照说法，plethora 偏贬）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ic 构成，医学生语指「多血质的」，现代口语指「过多的；过剩的」
复数形式，指多处「过剩」，使用频率很低
与医学义项同源的近义词，指局部充血，可与 plethora 对照记忆

senses.title: An excess of something
senses.definition: an amount of something that is far more than is needed, often more than can be used well
senses.definitionCN: 某物的数量远远超过所需，往往多到无法有效利用
senses.example: The city offers a plethora of restaurants near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 河边一带的餐馆多到数不过来。
senses.why: The medical word for too much blood was stretched to any overflowing supply, so the excess itself became the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 原本指「血液过多」的医学词被扩展到任何过剩的供给，于是「过量」本身成了词义。

senses.title: An abundance described in a neutral tone
senses.titleCN: 大量；丰富（中性或客套用法）
senses.definition: a great quantity of something, used neutrally when writers avoid sounding critical
senses.definitionCN: 某物的巨大数量；写作者不想显得挑剔时使用的中性说法
senses.example: There is a plethora of research on climate adaptation.
senses.exampleCN: 关于气候适应的研究数量非常多。
senses.why: Because the excess frame is weak in some contexts, the word slips into a polite synonym for a great many.
senses.whyCN: 在某些语境中「过剩」的意味很弱，这个词便滑向「许多」的客套说法。

senses.title: A medical excess of blood
senses.titleCN: 多血质；血容量过多（医学）
senses.definition: an old medical condition in which the body is thought to hold too much blood
senses.definitionCN: 古代医学认为体内血液过多的一种体质或病态
senses.example: Doctors once treated plethora by bleeding the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 医生过去靠给病人放血来治疗多血质。
senses.why: The Greek phrase stood for fullness of the blood and remained the literal sense in early medicine.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原短语表示「血液充盈」，在早期医学中保留了字面义。

intro.en: Plethora comes from late Latin plethora, from Greek plethore, a fullness or abundance, from pleres, full.
intro.cn: plethora 来自晚期拉丁语 plethora，源自希腊语 plethore（满盈、充盈），再来自 pleres（满的）。

items.en: Plethore names fullness or repletion, especially of the vessels.
items.cn: plethore 指满盈、充盈，尤指血管中的充盈。

items.en: Medical Latin borrows plethora as the name of a bodily condition.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语借入 plethora，用作一种体质或病名的名称。

items.en: English medical texts record plethora as the excess of blood.
items.cn: 英语医学文献把 plethora 记作血液过多。

items.en: Writers widen the word from blood to almost any kind of excess.
items.cn: 作家把该词从「血液」扩展到几乎任何事物的过剩。

items.en: In journalism plethora often merely means a great many, with a hint of criticism.
items.cn: 在现代新闻写作中，plethora 常只表示「很多」，并略带批评意味。

note.en: Plethora looks medical and sounds formal; compare the Latin fullness word pleres and the ordinary abundance nouns.
note.cn: plethora 带着医学色彩、读来正式；可与拉丁语「满」的 pleres 以及普通的「丰富」类名词对照。

entries.definition: full or attended by all members
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的（与 pleres 的「满」同根）

entries.definition: fully supplied or filled
entries.definitionCN: 充满的；饱足的（同出「填充」词根）

entries.definition: showing an excess
entries.definitionCN: 过多的；过剩的

entries.definition: a very large quantity of something
entries.definitionCN: 丰富；充裕（中性偏正面，不像 plethora 那样带批评）

entries.definition: more than is needed
entries.definitionCN: 剩余；盈余（强调「多出来的部分」）

entries.definition: far too much supply of something
entries.definitionCN: 供过于求；过剩（多用于商品市场）

normalIntro.en: Plethora keeps the Greek fullness in its bones: what is full beyond need becomes an excess.
normalIntro.cn: plethora 骨子里仍是希腊语的「满」：满过了需要，就变成过剩。

normal.en: A plethora of means a great many, often with a note of criticism.
normal.cn: 「a plethora of」表示大量，往往带一点批评意味。

normal.en: The -th- sound links plethora to its Greek origin, not to ple-, which belongs to other words.
normal.cn: 中间的 -th- 提示它来自希腊语，不要误把它归到别的 ple- 词族。

normal.en: Plethoric is the adjective, and in medicine it names a fullness of blood.
normal.cn: plethoric 是形容词，在医学中指血液充盈。

normal.en: Choose plethora when the amount is annoying and abundance when it is welcome.
normal.cn: 数量多到烦人时用 plethora，数量多到可喜时用 abundance。

normal.en: The word takes a singular verb: a plethora of problems lies ahead.
normal.cn: 它作主语时动词用单数，如「a plethora of problems」后面接 lies。

abstract.en: Picture a cup filled until the liquid stands above the rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子被倒满，液面高过杯沿。

abstract.en: See a table of menus so thick that no dish gets chosen.
abstract.cn: 想象一桌厚得翻不完的菜单，结果一道菜也没选成。

abstract.en: Think of an old doctor holding a bowl to catch the surplus blood.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老医生端着碗去接多余的血。

examples.en: There is a plethora of designs, yet none of them fits the brief.
examples.cn: 设计方案多得成堆，却没有一个符合要求。

examples.en: Critics complained of a plethora of unnecessary rules.
examples.cn: 批评者抱怨不必要的规定多如牛毛。

examples.en: The word plethora sounds formal in most British newspapers.
examples.cn: 在多数英国报纸里，plethora 读来相当正式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑了多啦」——东西多得扑了一地，就是过剩；这只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pleres（满的）+ -thore（充盈状态）→ plethore（满盈）→ 医学拉丁语 plethora（血液过多）→ 英语 plethora，核心义「满到过量」。

sensesIntro.en: Plethora starts as a medical name for too much blood, then any excess, and finally a neutral word for a great many.
sensesIntro.cn: plethora 最初是「血液过多」的医学术语，随后泛指任何过剩，最后又成为表示「很多」的中性词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dish heaped so high that it spills over the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘子堆得高过边缘，东西溢了出来。

branches.en: Any overflowing supply is the modern core sense.
branches.cn: 任何溢出的供给量都是现代核心义。

branches.en: The neutral use simply says a great many without blame.
branches.cn: 中性用法只表示「很多」，不带责备。

branches.en: The blood sense is the original medical sense.
branches.cn: 「血液过多」是最初的医学义。

branches.en: Both excess and abundance depend on the same full measure.
branches.cn: 「过剩」与「大量」都依赖同一个「满」的尺度。

branches.en: The blood condition is the literal body version of the same image.
branches.cn: 血液过多的病症是同一意象在身体上的字面版本。

intro.en: Plethora is a Greek-derived noun with a family of fullness words, from pleres to replete and surplus.
intro.cn: plethora 是源自希腊语的名词，与 pleres、replete、surplus 等表示「满」的词同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the Greek noun as plethora, and the Latin root plenus, full, also produced replete and supplement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语沿用希腊名词 plethora，拉丁语词根 plenus（满的）又派生出 replete 与 supplement。

items.example: Roughly this word supplies the image of fullness.
items.exampleCN: 大致是这个希腊词提供了「满」的意象。

items.example: The Greek noun already carried an excess of fluid.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词本就有「液体过多」之意。

items.example: The -thore ending marks the filled state.
items.exampleCN: 结尾表示被充满的状态。

items.example: Plenus is the Latin cousin of the Greek word.
items.exampleCN: plenus 是这个希腊词的拉丁亲族。

items.example: A plenary session means everyone is present.
items.exampleCN: 全体会议意味着每个人都到场。

items.example: A town replete with cafés has too many of them.
items.exampleCN: 咖啡馆「充满」的小镇就是咖啡馆太多。

items.meaning: something added to fill a gap
items.example: Supplement builds on the same filling root.
items.exampleCN: supplement 也建立在「填充」词根上。

items.example: Plethoric is the adjective built from this noun.
items.exampleCN: plethoric 是由这个名词构成的形容词。

items.example: Plenty is the everyday fullness noun.
items.exampleCN: plenty 是日常的「充足」名词。
